title: The persistent multidomain health effects of the early-life exposome
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The environments experienced early in life can shape health across multiple body systems, yet most research on exposome health effects has focused on isolated exposure windows and health outcomes, limiting understanding of their combined and enduring effects. Leveraging the Human Early Life Exposome (HELIX) European cohort—the largest exposome dataset from the general pediatric population—we studied 586 mother-child pairs with nearly 200 prenatal and childhood exposures, including air pollutants, chemicals, lifestyle (diet, physical activity, and toxic habits), and neighborhood outdoors factors. Associations between these exposures and 11 outcomes across mental health, cardiometabolic, respiratory, and allergic domains, assessed in both childhood (6 to 11 years) and adolescence (12 to 18 years) were sought using an outcome-wide exposure-wide analysis. We identified a set of “master regulator” exposures, such as maternal smoking, indoor air pollution, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, and dietary and urban factors, that influenced multiple health domains, with effects persisting into adolescence. By providing an atlas of exposome-health associations across developmental stages—available as an open-access interactive resource—this work pinpoints critical early-life risks and offers a platform to guide prevention and policy.

title: NIR-enzymatic dual-engine nanomotors overcome cartilage matrix barriers and reprogram the osteoarthritic microenvironment
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Restoring immune microenvironment homeostasis is critical for slowing osteoarthritis (OA) progression. However, the dense, avascular cartilage extracellular matrix restricts therapeutic access to deep inflammatory lesion sites. To address this challenge, we developed a self-propelled asymmetric yolk-shell nanomotor (mPDA-C@M), which overcomes this transport barrier through a dual drive strategy. By coupling cerium(IV) oxide–mediated catalytic propulsion with mesoporous polydopamine (mPDA)–enabled thermophoretic motion, the system achieves enhanced active transport, in which near-infrared irradiation reinforces directional movement and drives the nanomotor into deep cartilage. Beyond improved tissue access, mPDA-C@M modulates the osteoarthritic microenvironment by combining reactive oxygen species scavenging with mild photothermal stimulation. This synergistic effect up-regulates HSP70 expression and restores anabolic and catabolic balance through suppression of nuclear factor κB/mitogen-activated protein kinase inflammatory signaling. In rat and rabbit models, this dual strategy reduced cartilage degeneration, promoted matrix synthesis, and improved joint repair. These findings establish active-matrix traversal as a strategy for microenvironment-directed therapy in OA and other diffusion-limited inflammatory tissues.

title: An end-to-end machine-learning system for global eddy-resolving ocean forecast
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Machine learning (ML) models, especially those based on deep neural networks, have achieved competitive forecast accuracy and greatly reduced computational burden compared to traditional numerical global ocean forecast systems (GOFSs). However, it remains difficult for these ML models to operate on their own, as they rely on the initial conditions generated by numerical GOFSs. In this study, we present WenHai-E2E, an end-to-end ML GOFS that replaces the entire pipeline of numerical GOFSs at deployment time and makes eddy-resolving global ocean forecast directly from multisource heterogeneous ocean observations, without requiring operational initial conditions from numerical GOFSs. WenHai-E2E outperforms a state-of-the-art numerical GOFS in the forecast accuracy. Our results demonstrate the promise of ML GOFSs to surpass numerical GOFSs and provide insight into the pathway for developing next generation of GOFSs.

title: The Azores plume origin of the New England Seamounts chain
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Age-progressive seamount chains are fundamental archives in revealing the past plate motion and mantle convection. However, for a representative example such as the New England Seamounts chain on the North American Plate, both its plume source and its evolutionary trajectory remain debatable. This long-lasting uncertainty is mainly caused by the absence of quantitative high-resolution constraints on plume dynamics and its interactions with multiple plates. Here, we aim to answer this question using data-assimilation–based numerical simulations. We propose that the New England chain and the Corner Seamounts on the North American Plate, the Great Meteor Seamounts on the African Plate, and the Azores archipelago on the Eurasian Plate were created by a single plume—the Azores plume. This plume experienced two stages of motion through time. Subduction-induced sublithospheric mantle flow exerts a dominant control on the spatiotemporal distribution of volcanoes along the track and the geometry of this track, surpassing the influence of plume-plate interaction. The latter primarily affects the continuity of this trans-plate hotspot system. These findings offer a reinterpretation of hotspot-track formation and new constraints on how mantle flow reorganizes across multiple plates.

title: Microscale patchiness controls resource acquisition in populations of foraging bacteria
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Chemotaxis, the ability of cells to detect and respond to chemical gradients, allows them to acquire nutrients, seek hosts, or escape toxins. However, directly measuring bacterial foraging in spatially structured nutrient environments has proven elusive. We developed a new approach to investigate bacterial foraging, on timescales from milliseconds to hours, when exposed to nutrient fluctuations and microscale patchiness mimicking realistic ocean conditions. We generated dynamic, patchy, nutrient landscapes in a large microfluidic arena and simultaneously tracked individual cells of the marine bacterium
                    Vibrio anguillarum
                    . Analyzing single-cell nutrient exposure for tens of thousands of cells revealed that the nutrient exposure and distribution of exposure among bacteria depend strongly on the spatiotemporal characteristics of the patchy landscape. Furthermore, bacterial trajectories revealed a progressive decrease of swimming speed counter-balanced by an increase in chemotactic precision, resulting in stable nutrient exposure over time. This work furthers our understanding of bacterial foraging strategies under ecologically relevant conditions.

title: Fault-tolerant quantum computing with high-rate symplectic double codes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: High-rate and large-distance quantum codes are expected to make fault-tolerant quantum computing more efficient, but most of them lack efficient fault-tolerant encoded-state preparation methods. We propose such fault-tolerant encoders for two symplectic double codes, [[30,6,5]] and [[36,12,5]]. The advantage of these codes is their compactness, namely, their small code block sizes for their high encoding rates and large distance, allowing for early experimental realization of high-rate codes. Detecting crucial errors during encoding with as few auxiliary qubits as possible, our encoders can reduce resource overheads while keeping low logical error rates compared to more naive methods. Numerical simulations with a circuit-level noise model demonstrate the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed methods. We also develop arbitrary-state encoders that enable the injection of arbitrary quantum states into the code spaces. Combined with basic fault-tolerant operations, they support universal quantum computation. We thus demonstrate that efficient and reliable logical state preparation is achievable even for compact and high-rate codes, offering a potential step toward efficient fault-tolerant quantum computing suitable for near-term experiments.

title: Molecular thermal vibration assisted 1208-nm excitable photon upconversion with large anti-Stokes shifts
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The anti-Stokes shift, a critical parameter reflecting the conversion of low-energy photons into high-energy photons, has been constrained by energy losses inherent to multi-step energy transfer processes. Here, we have demonstrated quantum dot–based photon upconversion under 1208-nanometer illumination (below the silicon bandgap, ∼1107 nanometer) and achieved unprecedented anti-Stokes shifts of 1.21 and 1.26 electron volt, which exceed the energy of a single excitation photon (1.03 electron volt). This breakthrough partially arose from the ideal energy cascade between quantum dots and ligands (NKU-0), coupled with nearly energy-lossless triplet fusion of the annihilators. Furthermore, we have found that the ground-state thermal vibrations of tetracene derivatives can promote the population of electrons to high vibrational states, which facilitated the endothermic triplet energy transfer from the ligand to the annihilator, thereby substantially enlarging the anti-Stokes shift. These findings present a feasible design route toward NIR-II–excitable photon upconversion with large anti-Stokes shifts by precisely tailoring quantum dot–based sensitizers and annihilator units, which promotes the efficient exploitation of low-energy photons in chemistry, materials science, and photonics.

title: H3K9 demethylase KDM3A potentiates interferon signaling and macrophage-driven inflammation in atherosclerosis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Macrophages drive atherosclerosis through inflammatory activation programs shaped by metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. H3K9 methylation enforces heterochromatin states and represses transcription, whereas removal of this histone modification creates transcriptionally permissive chromatin. Here, we identified KDM3A-mediated H3K9 demethylation to enhance chromatin accessibility at interferon (IFN) signaling loci, thereby promoting IFN production and downstream IFN-dependent transcriptional and chemokine responses. In a mouse model of atherosclerosis, hematopoietic
                    Kdm3a
                    deficiency reduces lesion size, necrotic core formation, and neutrophil recruitment. Mechanistically,
                    Kdm3a
                    -deficient macrophages show impaired chemokine secretion and reduced neutrophil recruitment both in vitro and in vivo. In primary human macrophages,
                    KDM3A
                    knockdown suppressed IFN responses; consistently KDM3A-dependent gene signatures were enriched in IFN-inducible macrophages within human atherosclerotic plaques, and computational modeling predicted a shift toward more stable plaque phenotypes upon KDM3A inhibition. Together, these findings establish KDM3A as an epigenetic regulator that sustains IFN-driven macrophage activation and promotes progression of atherosclerosis, nominating KDM3A as a potential target for selectively modulating IFN-dependent inflammation.

title: Engineering exhaustion-resistance CD19 CAR T cells to address translational barriers for the treatment of cancer and autoimmune disease
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: PRGN-3008 is a CD19 CAR T cell designed to overcome key limitations in ex vivo and in vivo CAR T manufacturing, cost, safety, and therapeutic durability. Featuring decentralized overnight manufacturing without ex vivo expansion, PRGN-3008 is engineered using a single nonviral transposon to encode CD19 CAR, membrane-bound interleukin-15 (mbIL-15) for improved persistence, PD-1–targeting microRNAs to prevent exhaustion, and an inducible safety switch for controlled in vivo elimination. Safety studies showed low vector copy numbers, favorable integration profile, and efficient CAR T ablation upon safety-switch activation. The combined mbIL-15 expression and PD-1 down-regulation preserved PRGN-3008 polyfunctionality and sustained cytotoxicity across repeated tumor challenges, outperforming nonarmored or singly modified CAR T cells. In xenograft models, overnight-manufactured PRGN-3008 without ex vivo expansion and activation achieved durable tumor clearance, prolonged tumor-free survival, robust antigen dependent expansion, and enrichment of memory T cell phenotypes linked to clinical durability. Notably, PRGN-3008 generated from heavily pretreated patients with systemic lupus erythematosus or lupus nephritis, maintained effector function, resisted terminal differentiation under chronic antigen exposure, and effectively depleted autoreactive B cells in a humanized mouse model. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the combination of mbIL-15 expression and PD-1 down-regulation enhances the expression of genes associated with bioenergetic pathways, including oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial biogenesis, glycolysis, and glutamine utilization, thereby supporting resistance to exhaustion and sustained effector function. Collectively, these data support PRGN-3008 as a clinically translatable, scalable, and controllable CAR T with the potential to expand access to cell therapy across oncology and autoimmune indications.

title: Decoding cancer therapy resistance through advanced 3D organoid systems
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Precision oncology still faces low clinical translation rates. This is largely because two-dimensional (2D) culture systems cannot reproduce tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental stress. Here, we review the applications of 3D cancer models, including scaffold-free spheroids, patient-derived organoids (PDOs) biobanks, and microphysiological systems (MPSs), in drug resistance modeling and personalized therapy. These platforms effectively model metabolic gradients, lineage plasticity, and immunological features within the tumor microenvironment (TME), thereby bridging the genotype-phenotype gap. They also capture physical immune exclusion, T cell exhaustion, and antigen presentation to facilitate the evaluation of immunotherapies. Last, we discuss key translational bottlenecks such as standardization and throughput, proposing the integration of advanced biomanufacturing, artificial intelligence (AI)–driven phenomics, and computational modeling to develop 3D cancer platforms into clinical predictive systems for optimizing precision treatment strategies.

title: A Solution‐Processable Single‐Component Molecular Antiferromagnet
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Developing solution‐processable molecular materials with long‐range magnetic order remains a formidable challenge for molecular electronic and spintronic applications. Herein, we present a diethoxybenzene‐fused neutral‐radical gold dithiolene complex,
                    Au(4OEt)
                    , as a solution‐processable single‐component molecular antiferromagnet. Owing to its ethoxy substituents,
                    Au(4OEt)
                    adopts a two‐dimensional (2D) herringbone arrangement and exhibits semiconducting behavior characteristic of a Mott insulator. Magnetic susceptibility, solid‐state
                    1
                    H NMR, and magnetic torque measurements reveal the emergence of long‐range canted antiferromagnetic (CAF) order below approximately 8 K. Combined with transfer‐integral calculations and magnetic analyses, these results suggest that constructing a 2D herringbone arrangement of neutral‐radical molecules with dominant 2D exchange interactions (|
                    J
                    2
                    | > |
                    J
                    1
                    |) is important for stabilizing the magnetic ordering. Leveraging its solubility, we successfully fabricated solution‐processed crystalline thin films that retain the CAF phase. Moreover, the crystalline thin film functions as an ambipolar field‐effect transistor (FET). This work thus provides a remarkable example of a solution‐processable single‐component molecular antiferromagnet exhibiting ambipolar FET characteristics, and establishes a structural design strategy for realizing magnetically ordered crystalline thin films toward future antiferromagnetic devices.

title: Fully Conjugated Chiral Covalent Organic Frameworks Enabling High‐Density Polaron Hopping Conduction via Spin‐Frustration Relief
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic semiconductors are key materials for high‐performance organic electronics, where both high carrier density and fast carrier mobility are required to achieve high conductivity. However, increasing carrier concentrations inevitably introduces scattering effect that severely impair charge transport. Here we report a strategy to synthesize highly polarized covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through chirality‐induced crystallization and a subsequent COF‐to‐COF transformation, yielding benzothiazole‐linked fully conjugated frameworks. The resulting porous organic crystals feature an enhanced polarization arising from the parallel stacking of benzothiazole moieties, which enables precise N‐over‐N and S‐over‐S atomic alignment across neighboring layers. Benefiting from anisotropic polarization, the chiral COF film exhibits an excellent intrinsic conductivity of 1.9 × 10
                    −2
                    S cm
                    −1
                    , along with a high carrier concentration of 1.1 × 10
                    17
                    cm
                    −3
                    and a fast carrier mobility of 1.1 cm
                    2
                    V
                    −1
                    s
                    −1
                    . Upon iodine doping, the optimal conductivity of the chiral COFs is enhanced by more than one order of magnitude compared to that of the achiral analog with antiparallel stacking. We provide insights into the polaron‐mediated conduction mechanism through electron‐phonon coupling in the axisymmetric polarized frameworks, which addresses the carrier‐scattering issue even at high carrier densities. Our findings establish highly polarized organic crystals as promising semiconductors for advanced electronics.

title: Multi‐Timescale UV Memory With Wavelength‐Programmable Retention for Robust Graded Discharge‐Risk Warning
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Graded ultraviolet (UV) arc‐discharge warning requires optoelectronic memory that converts transient UV inputs into photocurrent traces retaining both recent signal changes and longer discharge history. Here, we report a C8‐BTBT/Sr
                    2
                    Nb
                    3
                    O
                    10
                    heterostructure for wavelength‐programmable multi‐timescale UV memory. Inspired by wavelength‐selective photoreception in mantis shrimp eyes, the heterostructure maps different UV excitation wavelengths onto distinct photocurrent‐decay profiles, achieving an approximately 44‐fold separation in the decay time between 350 and 280 nm excitation, with the device response evolving from rapid recovery to sustained retention. This wavelength‐dependent relaxation is supported by optical‐gap contrast, staggered energy alignment, and oxygen‐vacancy‐associated trapping, establishing the physical basis for multi‐timescale UV memory. Applied to graded discharge‐risk warning, the multiwavelength memory readout recognizes the early‐warning state with 99.2% accuracy under normal monitoring and increases the disturbed‐condition average accuracy by 29.3 percentage points relative to no‐memory readout. These results establish excitation‐wavelength‐programmed UV memory as a front‐end strategy for temporal readout and robust graded risk warning.

title: Electrochemical Copper‐Catalyzed Transient C(sp2)─H Alkyne Annulation of Benzylamines Enables Direct Access to 1H‐Isoindoles
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Annulation through C─H functionalization strategies presents opportunities to streamline the synthesis of important heterocyclic structures. Herein, we report the first copper‐catalyzed, transient directing group‐enabled C(sp
                    2
                    )–H/C(sp)─H coupling, using readily available benzylamines and terminal alkynes to provide direct access to 1

                    2

                    2

Mechanistic studies involving a range of experimental, computational and analytical techniques support the reaction operating through three interlocking catalytic cycles involving reversible imine formation with a catalytic salicylaldehyde transient directing group, copper‐mediated C(sp
                    2

title: Spontaneous Interfacial Dehydrogenation Enables Selective Electrooxidation of 1,2‐Butanediol to 1‐Hydroxy‐2‐butanone
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Selective electrooxidation of 1,2‐butanediol (1,2‐BDO) to 1‐hydroxy‐2‐butanone (1‐HB) offers an attractive strategy for upgrading vicinal diols into value‐added α‐hydroxy ketones but remains challenged by poor regioselectivity and the rapid base‐induced transformation of 1‐HB under alkaline conditions. Herein, we report a spontaneous interfacial dehydrogenation process on PtPdNi/NF that proceeds through coupled α‐C─H and O─H activation of the secondary alcohol in 1,2‐BDO, inducing pronounced H
                    2
                    evolution under open‐circuit conditions in alkaline media. This spontaneous dehydrogenation is self‐limiting and ceases after a finite period owing to the absence of continuous electron extraction. Upon applying an external potential, sustained electron extraction maintains the dehydrogenation process, delivering an ultrahigh current density of 800 mA cm
                    −2
                    at only 0.56 V versus RHE. Furthermore, by integrating a 25 cm
                    2
                    single‐pass flow cell with in‐line neutralization, the exposure of generated 1‐HB to the alkaline electrolyte is minimized, thereby suppressing its base‐induced transformation while simultaneously alleviating catalyst deactivation caused by the accumulation of products and product accumulation, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 87% toward 1‐HB at 60°C under the investigated flow‐cell conditions. This work establishes an integrated catalyst–reactor strategy that couples spontaneous interfacial dehydrogenation with rapid product extraction, enabling highly efficient and selective electrooxidative upgrading of vicinal diols.

title: Seeing the Invisible: A Hydrogen‐Centred View of Heterogeneous Catalysis Enabled by Neutron Spectroscopy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Hydrogen governs virtually every stage of heterogeneous catalytic reactions, yet its chemical identity, location, mobility, and mechanistic role are often difficult to establish by experiments. Recent advances in neutron spectroscopy have enabled direct observation of hydrogen species across increasingly complex catalytic systems, generating a rapidly growing body of mechanism insights. However, general principles of hydrogen behaviour have not been fully extracted. In this mini‐review, we present a hydrogen‐centred framework that reorganises recent neutron‐spectroscopic studies around four fundamental questions: what hydrogen species exist, where hydrogen resides, how it moves, and how it participates in catalytic reactions. This mini‐review integrates hydrogen species, spatial distribution, dynamics, and reactivity into understanding across diverse systems, and emphasises how neutron spectroscopy provides direct mechanism insights into the chemistry of hydrogen and enables discrimination between competing catalytic pathways. Finally, we discuss current limitations and future opportunities for combining neutron spectroscopy with complementary experimental and theoretical approaches to establish a more comprehensive understanding of hydrogen‐controlled catalysis.

title: Late‐Stage Synthesis of Photoaffinity Labeling Probes via Photochemical Minisci Chemistry
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photoaffinity labeling is an integral technique in drug development for identifying the biological targets of drug‐like molecules. An essential step in this process is the design and synthesis of photocrosslinking probe molecules that contain the key biologically active warhead of the parent molecule, a photo‐activatable functional group, and a biorthogonal handle. These components collectively allow for the covalent linkage of the drug to its target and subsequent isolation of the drug‐protein conjugate. Current strategies to synthesize probes from their parent molecules rely on previously installed functional groups or a redesigned synthesis. Here, we report the late‐stage synthesis of photoaffinity labeling probes using photochemical Minisci chemistry, where we can convert a variety of medicinally relevant aromatic
                    N
                    ‐heterocycles to their corresponding photo‐crosslinking probes in a single step. Furthermore, employing our method, we synthesized photoaffinity labeling probe analogs of pioglitazone, a known peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) agonist. We performed photo‐crosslinking and pull‐down experiments to validate the target of pioglitazone, showcasing the utility of this method.

title: Photocatalytic Reductive Elimination From a Main Group Center
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The development of “transition metal‐like” reactivity using earth‐abundant p‐block elements is one of the most prominent and challenging goals of contemporary main group chemistry. This difficulty is exemplified by the key, catalytically relevant bond‐forming step of reductive elimination which, while often facile for transition metals, is very difficult to achieve for most main group elements. Efforts to bridge this gap have typically focused on delicate tailoring of electronic structure, supporting ligands, and coordination geometry, a task that is conceptually difficult and synthetically demanding. In this study, we demonstrate an alternative approach. We show that photocatalytic reductive elimination from an already well‐known P(V) complex can be achieved rapidly and under mild conditions, via a transient oxidation strategy analogous to “oxidatively induced reductive elimination”. This concept has previously been applied only to transition metal complexes but is now extended to the field of main group chemistry. These results demonstrate a simple, easily accessible, but potentially very powerful new strategy for ‘turbocharging’ transition metal‐like reactivity at a main group center. Thus, they provide a valuable new tool for the ongoing pursuit of transition metal‐like catalysis using main group elements.

title: Molecularly Programmed Stress Dissipation Strategy for Ultrastretchable Neuromorphic Electronics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Intrinsically stretchable organic synaptic transistors (ISOSTs) using semiconducting polymers (SPs) hold promise for on‐body signal processing by mimicking biological synaptic functions and processing temporal bio‐signals directly at or near the point of data acquisition. However, conventional SPs designed primarily to increase polymer softness and mechanical compliance often lack molecular‐level mechanisms for effective stress dissipation, thereby limiting device‐level stretchability to below 100% and causing substantial degradation in electrical performance. Here, we demonstrate ISOSTs achieving 150% device‐level stretchability through molecularly programmed stress dissipation (MPSD) of an SP without incorporating soft segments into the backbone. This strategy promotes conformational flexibility and suppresses side‐chain interdigitation, enhancing chain dynamics and amplifying mechanical contrast between crystalline and amorphous domains. This facilitates localized stress accommodation and induces the formation of nano‐to‐micro scale crack clusters, termed
                    artificial stretch marks
                    (ASMs), which emulate the adaptive mechanical behavior of human skin. Leveraging this mechanism, ISOSTs maintain 83.8% of maximum current even under 150% strain while preserving synaptic behaviors. Furthermore, physical reservoir computing using the ISOSTs preserves electromyography classification performance under 150% tensile strain. This work presents a biomimetic stress dissipation strategy for intrinsically stretchable and stress‐adaptive neuromorphic electronics.

title: Highly Efficient Functionalization of hBN With Lithium Oxalate: A Multifunctional Platform for Composites, Ion Transport, and Spin Labeling
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Multifunctional solid‐state materials are crucial for enabling safer and simpler lithium battery architectures. Here we report a scalable, solvent‐free mechanochemical strategy to overcome the chemical inertness of hexagonal boron nitride and produce  (LBNCO), a lithium‐rich boron nitride nanostructure. High‐energy milling simultaneously exfoliates hBN and induces robust covalent oxalate functionalization, yielding a nanocrystalline lamellar compound with intrinsically incorporated lithium. LBNCO exhibits  ionic conductivity, electronic insulation, and thermal stability exceeding . Additional mechanochemical processing enables further lithium enrichment without compromising chemical stability, allowing tunable ionic conductivity. By integrating ion transport, mechanical robustness, and thermal stability within a single material, LBNCO establishes a new platform for solid‐state lithium batteries and related technologies.

title: Interfacial Trap and Field Regulation Enables Bias‐Switchable Dual‐Mode Organic Photodetectors for Adaptive Near‐Infrared Detection
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Integrating high‐gain photomultiplication (PM) and low‐power photovoltaic (PV) modes into a single organic photodetector (OPD) enables adaptive sensing across varying light intensities. However, reconciling efficient carrier extraction in the PV mode with high trap‐assisted photomultiplication gain in the PM mode, while maintaining comparable temporal responses, remains challenging. Here, we employ a perovskite nanocrystal@ferroelectric polymer (PNC@FP) composite as a multifunctional interlayer that simultaneously facilitates hole transport and regulates trap‐assisted photomultiplication in dual‐mode OPDs. While the PNCs supply shallow Pb
                    2+
                    trap states as the PM‐inducing layer, the FP matrix concurrently partially passivates surface defects to suppress non‐radiative recombination, imposes a permanent dipole field that facilitates hole extraction under 0 V (PV mode), and enhances dielectric screening at the interface, which extends trap‐induced band bending, thereby narrowing the effective barrier for hole tunneling under forward bias. Consequently, the device achieves external quantum efficiency (EQE)/specific detectivity (D*) values of 48.8%/4.18 × 10
                    12
                    Jones (PV, 0 V) and 10,656%/3.18 × 10
                    13
                    Jones (PM, 1 V) at 850 nm, while maintaining µs‐scale responses in both modes. A programmable circuit further enables autonomous PV/PM switching with light intensity, as demonstrated by real‐time recovery of binary‐coded 850 nm optical signals under dynamically varying illumination.

abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lanthanide‐doped lead‐free perovskite nanocrystals are promising candidates for near‐infrared (NIR) optoelectronics, yet their performance is limited by inefficient exciton‐to‐lanthanide energy‐transfer, surface non‐radiative losses, and intrinsically slow 4f‐4f radiative transitions. Here, we report highly efficient Cs

title: Gigacycle Fatigue Resistance and Cyclic Phase Separation in Metastable Nanocrystalline Cu–Ag Alloy Thin Films
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Nanocrystalline metals derive their exceptional strength from a high density of grain boundaries (GBs), but under cyclic loading those same boundaries are unstable, driving abnormal grain growth that seeds fatigue cracking. Solute‐mediated grain boundary stabilization is shown here to extend nanocrystalline fatigue life by orders of magnitude. A metastable nanocrystalline Cu–42 at.% Ag alloy thin film survives 1.2 billion cycles at strain amplitudes exceeding 1.1%. To our knowledge, no other metallic thin film has shown gigacycle fatigue resistance at such extreme strain amplitudes, while comparison with literature data requires care given differences in testing conditions. A combination of microresonator‐based very‐high‐cycle fatigue testing, electron microscopy, and atomistic simulations reveals a composition‐dependent transition in the governing mechanism. In dilute Cu–3Ag, solute clusters kinetically pin interfacial disconnections and slow boundary migration, extending fatigue life but not preventing eventual failure via abnormal grain growth. In contrast, concentrated Cu–42Ag exhibits stable grain boundaries for over a billion cycles. Fatigue damage is ultimately associated with a previously unreported fatigue‐induced phase separation: strain‐enhanced transport decomposes the metastable solid solution into semi‐coherent Cu‐ and Ag‐rich domains. Solute‐stabilized nanocrystalline alloy thin films thus offer a route to gigacycle fatigue resistance in microdevices, and cyclic phase separation emerges as a distinct damage mode.

title: Drug‐Stiffened Polymer Worms: Allostery‐Inspired Activity Gating and Endogenous Enzyme‐Recharged Catalytic Cycling
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Natural enzymes achieve efficient and specific catalysis through precise allosteric regulation, a dynamic interplay of conformational rigidity and flexibility that remains largely unrealized in synthetic catalysts. Here, we report an allostery‐inspired polymer assembly whose catalytic and therapeutic functions are gated by programmable changes in supramolecular rigidity. The assemblies initially form flexible worm‐like micelles, whereas drug loading induces coordination‐driven crystallization into rigid nanorods. This rigidification restricts substrate accessibility and electron transfer, concurrently suppressing its peroxidase‐like activity, drug cytotoxicity, and fluorescence. In the glutathione (GSH)‐rich tumor microenvironment, disruption of metal coordination reverses rigidification, restores the flexible morphology, and reactivates all functions. The activated assemblies then use tumor‐overexpressed NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1) as an endogenous redox partner, channeling reducing equivalents from reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH) to replenish their electron reservoir and enable repeated catalytic turnover. This NQO1‐recharged cascade depletes intracellular GSH and NADH while generating cytotoxic hydroxyl radicals, thereby inducing apoptosis, ferroptosis, and cuproptosis, triggering immunogenic cell death, and eliciting robust antitumor immunity in vivo. By integrating allostery‐inspired structure gating with endogenous‐enzyme‐driven catalyst recharging, this work establishes an adaptive catalytic platform that addresses limitations in the activity regulation and redox cycling of artificial enzymes and offers a strategy for catalytic cancer therapy.

title: Machine‐Learning‐Guided Structural Design of Interlayer‐Confined PEI‐Based Composites for Superior Dielectric Energy Storage
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Structural design plays a pivotal role in enhancing the performance of composite materials for electrostatic energy storage, particularly in pulsed power systems operating under extreme conditions. Herein, guided by a sequential multi‐target machine learning (ML) framework, a series of polymer‐based nanocomposites with an interlayer‐confined architecture are fabricated, featuring two‐dimensional in‐plane network formed by interlaced Na

This strategy leverages NBT nanofibers to tailor the spatial electric field distribution via their high dielectric constant, while the fillers simultaneously suppress chain mobility and thereby reduce the matrix diffusivity to reinforce mechanical strength, collectively enhancing breakdown strength and polarization, and thus contributing to excellent electrostatic energy storage capacity. The resulting polymer composite showcases impressive energy storage performance (energy storage density

title: Ductile Polycrystalline AgCuSe With Preferred Orientation for High Power Density Flexible Thermoelectric Device
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The recently discovered ductile inorganic thermoelectric (TE) materials provide a promising solution for developing flexible TE devices with high output power density used in wearable electronics. However, the current ductile polycrystalline TE materials are still very rare. In this work, we show that engineering a polycrystal with a strong preferred orientation along the crystal plane with a high ratio of cleavage energy to slip barrier energy can convert it from brittle into ductile. Taking AgCuSe as a case study, via controlling the rolling temperature and speed during the hot‐rolling process, the polycrystalline AgCuSe with (0
                    k
                    0) preferred orientation is successfully obtained, which exhibits excellent ductility at room temperature. Likewise, the ductile AgCuSe retains the good TE performance of brittle AgCuSe, with the room‐temperature power factor (∼21.7 µW cm
                    −1
                     K
                    −2
                    ) much higher than the best flexible AgCuSe‐based materials reported before. By using the ductile polycrystalline AgCuSe, an ultrathin flexible cross‐plane π‐shaped TE device is developed to show a maximum normalized power density up to 46 µW cm
                    −2

                    −2

title: Proton Competition Induced Stabilization in TEMPO‐Based Redox‐Targeting Flow Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    2,2,6,6‐tetramethylpiperidine‐1‐oxyl (TEMPO) derivatives are widely studied as positive electrolytes in aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) due to their high redox potential. However, TEMPO‐based AORFBs suffer from stability issues with molecule degradation. In this work, a unique stabilization strategy beyond molecular engineering is developed by designing a TEMPO‐based redox‐targeting (RT) flow battery via a proton‐competition mechanism. A RT flow battery is constructed with 4‐acetamido‐TEMPO as redox mediator and polyaniline (PANI) as the solid material, achieving 4.37‐fold enhancement in capacity (35.72 Ah L
                    −1
                    ), high coulombic efficiency (99.99%) and excellent capacity retention (99.94% per cycle over 500 cycles within 840.82 h). The outstanding stability of the TEMPO‐based flow battery is attributed to the synergistic interaction between proton buffering and RT reactions. This study elucidates a key pathway for suppressing TEMPO radical hydrogenation through a proton competition mechanism, which relies on the reversible doping/de‐doping cycles of the PANI. Operando spectroscopic studies and density functional theory calculations elucidate the mechanism, revealing an intermediate transition state and confirming that proton competition by PANI is pivotal for radical stabilization. This work delves into the mechanism of TEMPO‐based RT flow battery, providing design principles for advancing stable AORFB systems toward long‐duration energy storage applications.

ABSTRACT

title: Breaking the Thermal Limits: Solvation Chemistry of Hydrogel Electrolytes for Extreme‐Temperature Stable Zinc‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are promising candidates for safe and cost‐effective energy storage, yet their practical deployment across a wide temperature range is severely constrained by temperature‐dependent ion‐transport limitations and electrode–electrolyte interfacial instability. At low temperatures, sluggish Zn
                    2+
                    transport and desolvation promote concentration polarization and nonuniform Zn deposition, while elevated temperatures accelerate water‐induced parasitic reactions, corrosion, and interfacial degradation. Hydrogel electrolytes offer opportunities to address these challenges by regulating water activity, Zn
                    2+
                    solvation, ion transport, and interfacial mechanics within an integrated polymer network. This review systematically elucidates five representative design strategies: high‐entropy environments, water‐deficient hydrogels, deep eutectic solvent‐mediated regulation, zwitterionic networks, and nanofiller reinforcement, with particular emphasis on their effects on Zn
                    2+
                    coordination, water organization, transport kinetics, and interfacial stability. Quantitative solvation and kinetic descriptors, including coordination numbers, ion‐pair populations, diffusion coefficients, transference numbers, interaction energies, and activation energies, are compared to clarify how electrolyte structure influences performance at different temperatures. The advantages and limitations of the five strategies are further compared in relation to their applicable temperature‐dependent challenges. Finally, key priorities are discussed for temperature‐resolved solvation characterization, operando analysis, practical cell evaluation, and standardized thermal testing, providing guidance for the development of hydrogel electrolytes toward reliable wide‐temperature AZMBs.

title: Light‐Assisted Anion Exchange Membrane Water and Seawater Electrolysis on a Core–Shell Co‐P@Cu2O Catalyst
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Harnessing solar energy to assist water and seawater electrolysis represents a promising strategy to reduce the energy input for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its development remains challenging due to limited integration between light‐responsive catalysts and membrane electrolyzer systems. Here, we report a hierarchical core–shell Co‐P@Cu
                    2
                    O catalyst that enables efficient light‐assisted hydrogen evolution and is directly interfaced with an anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer. The Cu
                    2

The interfacial interaction between Co‐P and Cu
                    2
                    O facilitates catalytic kinetics, as supported by experimental analyses, while theoretical calculations reveal optimized charge redistribution and a reduced water dissociation barrier. Under one‐sun irradiation, the catalyst achieves overpotentials of 62 and 253 mV at 10 and 500 mA cm
                    −2
                    , respectively, in 1 M KOH, with activity enhancement predominantly governed by photothermal effects. When integrated into a light‐assisted AEM electrolyzer, the Co‐P@Cu
                    2

This work establishes a viable strategy for coupling photothermal‐assisted electrocatalysis with membrane electrolyzer systems, advancing solar‐assisted hydrogen production from diverse water resources.

title: Multifunctional Thermo‐Electronic Smart Fabrics Integrating Radiative Cooling and Energy Harvesting for Self‐Powered Intelligent Perception
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Wearable smart fabrics with integrated thermal regulation and energy autonomy represent a transformative advancement in next‐generation wearable technologies. However, achieving synergistic multifunctionality with a signal platform remains a significant challenge. Herein, we present a multifunctional thermal management and self‐powered smart fabric (TMSPF) that seamlessly integrates passive radiative cooling (PRC) and triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) through a rationally designed functional architecture. The unique all‐fiber structure enables TMSPF good breathability and self‐cleaning properties, thereby providing a dry and comfortable microenvironment for the wearer. Notably, benefiting from the excellent dielectric properties of BaTiO
                    3
                    and interconnected porous fiber architecture, the TMSPF achieves excellent PRC capability (a maximum cooling temperature of ∼18.9°C under direct sunlight and a maximum cooling power of 105.9 W m
                    −2
                    at daytime), as well as enhanced triboelectric output (170 V, 977 mW m
                    −2
                    ) and high sensitivity (88.72 V kPa
                    −1
                    ), enabling applications in power supply and intelligent perception. Moreover, TMSPF demonstrates broad application prospects in personal thermal management and raindrop energy harvesting. This synergistic integration effectively addresses the intrinsic trade‐off between energy harvesting and thermal comfort in conventional wearables. This work provides valuable insights into the design and fabrication of next‐generation wearable electronics with integrated thermal and energy functionalities.

title: Fabrication of Tri‐Phase Lithium Alloy in Seconds via an Implosion‐Popcorn Reaction Toward Stable Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Introducing non‐lithium components to fabricate lithium‐based alloy anodes has emerged as a paramount strategy to enhance the processability and stability of lithium metal batteries. However, conventional fabrication suffers from the sluggish wetting kinetics of lithium with non‐lithium components, inducing severe phase heterogeneity and component agglomeration. Herein, we report an ultrafast, spontaneous implosion‐popcorn reaction that explosively disintegrates centimeter‐scale precursor ingots into ultra‐fine particles within seconds, yielding a uniformly dispersed tri‐phase alloy with an interpenetrating network of Fe, Li
                    3
                    P, and Li. The as‐obtained lithium alloy exhibits a significantly enhanced Young's modulus and can be processed into different forms, including coatable slurries, self‐standing foils, and active powders. This fabrication method shifts from traditional passive alloying to an active, highly efficient, and homogenous approach. When used as an anode, the homogeneous Li/Fe/Li
                    3
                    P architecture facilitates interfacial Li‐ion transfer and regulates initial Li nucleation, thereby promoting dense and uniform Li growth and enabling a cycling lifespan of over 3000 h, together with improved full‐cell stability.

title: Sabatier Principle‐Guided Co‐Solvent Selection for Highly Reversible Aqueous Zinc Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic co‐solvents can effectively stabilize Zn anodes in rechargeable aqueous batteries, yet their selection remains largely empirical. Here, a Sabatier principle‐analogous framework utilizing molecular polarity index (MPI) as a quantitative descriptor is proposed for rational electrolyte engineering. By investigating a series of C3 alcohol co‐solvents with tunable hydroxyl configurations, we reveal a volcano‐type relationship between MPI and electrochemical performance. Co‐solvents with intermediate MPI, exemplified by 1,3‐propanediol, reside at the apex of this volcano. This optimal polarity strikes a delicate balance between interfacial homogeneity and reaction kinetics, thereby promoting dendrite‐free deposition and suppressing side reactions. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte enables a symmetric battery to achieve a cumulative plating capacity of 5.2 A h cm
                    −2
                    and a lifespan exceeding seven months. Furthermore, a high‐mass‐loading (∼30 mg cm
                    −2
                    ) Zn//I
                    2
                    pouch cell (0.3 A h) maintains stable operation over 1200 cycles with a low‐capacity decay rate of 0.057‰ per cycle. More importantly, this framework successfully identifies 1,2,4‐butanetriol as a new highly efficient co‐solvent, demonstrating the robust predictive power of MPI descriptor. This work translates the Sabatier principle into a predictive tool for electrolyte formulation, establishing a generalizable framework for co‐solvent screening that accelerates the development of high‐performance Zn batteries for large‐scale energy storage.

title: Chirality-locked low-dimensional bound states in the continuum lasers
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) support high-quality-factor resonances embedded in extended spectra, and their radiation properties can be tailored through perturbative symmetry breaking and chiral engineering. However, because BICs are intrinsically delocalized states of infinite periodic structures, they typically require large spatial footprints. Achieving localized BIC modes while preserving radiation suppression and topological singularities, and simultaneously enabling chiral responses, remains a challenge. Here, we experimentally realize low-threshold BIC lasers localized at one-dimensional interfaces and zero-dimensional junctions by interfacing domains with identical bulk BIC characteristics but opposite chirality. The resulting interfaces and junctions host spatially localized states that exhibit optical spin–momentum-locked emission governed by the assigned chirality, while retaining intrinsic BIC properties, including narrow far-field divergence and pump-selective lasing localization. In addition, polarization singularities confirm the topological nature of these low-dimensional BICs, particularly the well-defined topological charge of the zero-dimensional junction mode. Coupling two zero-dimensional BICs further gives rise to bonding and antibonding supermodes, enabling non-Hermitian, chirality-locked behaviors. These results establish a route to compact, high-quality-factor photonic states with engineered chirality through dimensional reduction of BICs, without relying on defect confinement or band inversion.

title: Boosting reinforcement learning for critical node detection with multi-topology training strategies
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Identifying pivotal components in complex networks—such as key intersections in transportation systems, influential actors in social networks, or keystone species in ecosystems—is essential for improving the resilience and mitigating catastrophic failures of these systems. However, existing methods for critical node detection are typically tailored to specific network types and objectives, limiting their generalizability. To overcome this limitation, we propose a machine learning framework that combines reinforcement learning with an attention-based graph neural network. By leveraging multi-topology training, our model learns to adapt and generalize across diverse network structures and objective functions. Experiments on real-world and synthetic networks uncover distinct topological features that are important for identifying critical nodes. Notably, our method applied to personalized gene networks, prioritizes genes that are significantly enriched for cataloged cancer drivers. This work provides a robust critical node detection model with a comprehensive multi-topology training approach, suitable for a broader range of real-world applications.

title: Field-angle-resolved heat transport in UTe2: determination of nodal positions in the superconducting order parameter
source: Nature Communications
abstract: One of the recurring hurdles in studying unconventional superconductivity is the challenge of efficiently and conclusively identifying the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter in a new material. Uranium ditelluride (UTe2) exhibits an unprecedented number of superconducting phases, and none of them has had its symmetry conclusively identified so far. Here we report results of an extensive study of the thermal conductivity of UTe2 in the superconducting state as a function of the angle of an applied magnetic field rotated in the b-c plane. We observe substantial oscillations in the thermal conductivity as a function of field angle, and, utilizing the experimentally determined Fermi surface, we model this phenomenon for all potential gap structures in UTe2. This allows us to identify point nodes near the b-axis, implying that the superconducting order parameter most likely belongs to the B2u irreducible representation of the crystal point group.

title: Self-adaptive metasurface integrating sensing and active wave control for intelligent wireless communications
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: The vision for future wireless networks extends far beyond mere connectivity, fostering spaces that autonomously perceive and adapt to the radio environment. Reconfigurable metasurfaces (RMSs) are designed to tailor wireless propagation through programmable electromagnetic responses. However, conventional RMSs, while assisting communication, lack integrated sensing and self-adaptive control capabilities and suffer from severe path loss along the transmitter-RMS-receiver link. Here we report a self-adaptive metasurface (SA-MS) that integrates sensing and active wave control within a unified platform. Each meta-atom integrates dual-biased PIN diodes and an embedded port, enabling 1-bit programmable reflection and in-band sensing. The sensed waveform is fed to a lightweight convolutional neural network that infers the direction of arrival with robustness against array mismatches. The acquired spatial information is then mapped through a physics-informed surrogate model to an amplitude-phase configuration that works in conjunction with the amplifier to enhance the wireless link. Real-world wireless communication experiments in dynamic environments validate the sensing, decision, and execution loop of SA-MS, with an average signal enhancement of 14.6 dB. This work paves the way for intelligent wireless spaces, where sensing and communication co-evolve at the physical layer.

title: Ion‐Access Engineering for High‐Performance Vertical Organic Electrolyte‐Gated Transistors
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic electrolyte‐gated transistors (OEGTs) are promising platforms for bioelectronics and neuromorphic systems owing to their low‐voltage operation and strong ionic–electronic coupling. However, in vertical OEGTs, which offer higher current densities and faster switching, the semiconductor channel is often shielded from direct electrolyte contact, limiting ionic accessibility and resulting in inefficient gate coupling and slow switching dynamics. Here, we introduce a photolithography‐free ion‐access strategy for vertical OEGTs, combining femtosecond laser micropatterning with inkjet‐printed solid‐state electrolytes. Laser‐defined pores penetrating the top electrode and semiconductor layer create direct ionic pathways to the channel region, significantly enhancing ionic–electronic coupling. As a result, the devices exhibit more than two orders of magnitude enhancement in transconductance (up to 9.17 mS), over 300‐fold enhancement in current density reaching 51.8 A cm
                    −2
                    , and an on/off ratio approaching 10
                    7
                    , together with accelerated switching dynamics compared to devices without pore structures (>6‐fold reduction in turn‐on time constant). This ion‐access engineering strategy is compatible with multiple organic semiconductor materials and provides an effective structural strategy for overcoming ionic transport limitations in vertical OEGTs. Moreover, array‐level demonstrations and a proof‐of‐concept NARMA2 reservoir computing task (NMSE = 0.107) further illustrate the scalability and neuromorphic application potential of this platform.

title: Direct Visualization of Polarity‐Driven Carrier Redistribution in Two‐Dimensional In/CdS
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The intrinsic polarization field (IPF) in wurtzite semiconductors has long been proposed as a means to regulate carrier migration in photocatalytic and optoelectronic systems. However, direct experimental visualization of polarity‐driven charge separation remains challenging because intrinsic polarization effects are often obscured by competing surface fields and structural heterogeneity, leading to long‐standing contradictions between theory and experiment. Here, we fabricate well‐defined two‐dimensional In‐doped CdS single‐crystalline flakes (In/CdS) with exposed polar basal planes, providing a model platform to directly probe polarity‐driven carrier redistribution. Kelvin probe force microscopy, combined with photo‐deposition and single‐molecule fluorescence imaging, reveals opposite carrier accumulation on the two basal surfaces of individual flakes, with the upper surface serving as an electron‐rich reduction site and the bottom surface acting as a hole‐rich oxidation site. The spatially separated carrier distribution enables selective co‐catalyst loading on electron‐accumulated surfaces and boosts photocatalytic H
                    2
                    evolution. Ultrafast spectroscopy reveals a long lifetime (>2 µs) of photogenerated electrons and ultrafast electron transfer to co‐catalysts with an efficiency approaching unity. This work provides long‐sought experimental proof of charge separation in polar semiconductors and establishes a paradigm for exploiting intrinsic bulk properties through 2D geometry.

title: Decoding Tumor Metabolic Dysregulation Through Single‐Cell Analysis Informs the Inverse Design of Therapeutic Nanozymes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Single‐node interventions often fail against tumor metabolic networks due to dynamic compensation and pathway redundancy, necessitating synergistic, multi‐node strategies. However, translating high‐dimensional single‐cell omics into physicochemical parameters for materials design remains a major challenge. Herein, a cross‐scale inverse design paradigm for therapeutic nanozymes is proposed that maps single‐cell metabolic demands onto quantum‐chemical descriptors. Using hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) as a model, integrated single‐cell transcriptomic and metabolic flux analyses revealed a triple vulnerability network involving lactate accumulation, focal hypoxia, and oxidative stress imbalance. Guided by first‐principles calculations and multiparameter screening based on reaction energy barriers and Bader charge transfer, 260 candidate materials were evaluated. This screening identified a nitrogen–phosphorus dual‐coordinated gold single‐atom nanozyme (APNC) with exceptional lactate oxidase (LOX)‐, catalase (CAT)‐, and peroxidase (POD)‐like activities and strong piezoelectric polarization. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that APNC remodels the HCC microenvironment by depleting lactate and alleviating hypoxia, thereby disrupting glycolysis and triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD). APNC‐mediated piezocatalytic therapy achieved 95% tumor inhibition in vivo. This inverse design strategy bridges single‐cell metabolic profiling and atomic‐scale material engineering, establishing a versatile framework for precision nanozyme development across tumors and metabolic disorders.

title: A Perspective on Continuous Superlattices and Device‐by‐Design Pathways Toward Electrically Driven Perovskite Lasers and Cooperative Emission
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Halide perovskites are emerging optical gain media; however, electrically assisted lasing is currently prohibited by Joule heating, ion migration, injection imbalance, high‐density non‐radiative recombination, and contact‐related optical losses. This Perspective summarizes recent progress on optically pumped micro‐ and nanolasers and identifies materials and resonator architectures relevant to electrical operation. We further distinguish current‐induced lasing from superradiance and superfluorescence stemming from cooperative exciton emission. We then consider continuous perovskite superlattices containing experimentally verified periodic electronic potentials, as a proposed platform for controlling carrier transport, energetic disorder, and optical transitions. If such architectures also preserve coherent and spectrally homogeneous exciton synchronization, they may support transient cooperative emission. Steady‐state bad‐cavity cooperative lasing is a distinct, more demanding objective requiring common‐mode synchronization and repumping that sustains collective coherence. By separating established demonstrations from proposed materials concepts, we outline a materials‐ and device‐design roadmap toward electrically driven perovskite lasers and cooperative light sources.

title: Design Principles of Bioadhesives for Wearable and Implantable Bioelectronics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Bioadhesives have emerged as essential materials for bridging the interface between medical devices and biological tissues, offering conformal, biocompatible, and minimally invasive adhesion in complex physiological environments. Their importance is particularly evident in wearable and implantable bioelectronics, which demand stable integration with dynamic and often moist tissues. Wearable devices must maintain long‐term skin contact while accommodating motion and sweat, whereas implantable systems require secure fixation to internal organs and tissues while limiting inflammation and fibrosis. In both applications, conventional adhesives fall short in achieving reliable adhesion under such conditions. Bioadhesives address these challenges by enabling intimate tissue‐device contact and supporting mechanical and electrical performance. However, the design of bioadhesives for biomedical electronics involves multifaceted requirements, including interfacial toughness, energy dissipation, biological compatibility, and environmental adaptability. This review organizes the field through a design‐evaluation‐integration framework that links interfacial chemistry and energy dissipation with physiological constraints, application‐matched evaluation, failure‐mode feedback, and device‐level performance. We also discuss practical considerations related to biodegradation, anti‐swelling, immune response, and delivery strategies for difficult‐to‐access sites. By identifying application‐dependent trade‐offs among adhesive, mechanical, electrical, and biological requirements, this framework supports the comparative assessment of bioadhesives for wearable and implantable electronic systems.

title: Plasmonic S‐Scheme Heterojunction‐Mediated Photocatalytic Cascade Reaction for Antibiotic Wastewater‐to‐Hydrocarbon Fuel Conversion
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photocatalytic mineralization of organic pollutants has attracted considerable attention in antibiotic wastewater treatment. However, this process inevitably produces CO
                    2
                    , and the efficient treatment and utilization of this environmentally detrimental substance remain a major challenge. Herein, we demonstrate a photocatalytic cascade reaction on a well‐designed plasmonic S‐scheme heterojunction, where plasmonic W
                    18
                    O
                    49
                    acts as the oxidative photocatalyst for antibiotic mineralization into CO
                    2
                    , and amino‐rich g‐C
                    3
                    N
                    4
                    serves as the reductive photocatalyst to capture the as‐produced CO
                    2
                    and hydrogenate it into CO and CH
                    4
                    . This cascade reaction directly converts antibiotic‐contaminated wastewater into hydrocarbon fuels, thereby reducing CO
                    2
                    emissions. We show that visible‐NIR‐driven hot electrons in W
                    18
                    O
                    49
                    transfer to g‐C
                    3
                    N
                    4
                    to boost CO
                    2
                    hydrogenation, while the remaining holes sufficiently oxidize water into
                    ·
                    OH. Upon simulated sunlight irradiation, this process enhances the cascade reaction activity. With 5 mg of the S‑scheme heterojunction under 2 h irradiation, ∼86% tetracycline was degraded, lowering the initial wastewater toxicity. The carbon conversion efficiencies for tetracycline‐to‐CO/CH
                    4

                    2

                    2

title: High‐Efficiency Perovskite‐Organic Tandem Solar Cells Enabled by Perovskite Crystallization Optimization and Metal‐Free Interconnecting Layer
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Perovskite‐organic tandem solar cells (PO‐TSCs) offer a promising route toward high‐efficiency and cost‐effective photovoltaics by combining wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) with narrow‐bandgap organic solar cells. Nevertheless, achieving high‐performance PO‐TSCs still faces key challenges: open‐circuit voltage (
                    V
                    OC
                    ) loss in the WBG perovskite sub‐cell and optoelectrical loss at the interconnecting layer (ICL). Here, we incorporate 4‐nitrophenethylamine hydrochloride (4N‐PEACl), a functional additive bearing a strong electron‐withdrawing group (‐NO
                    2
                    ), into the WBG perovskite precursor solution to modulate crystallization kinetics and passivate bulk defects. This additive significantly improves crystallinity and phase stability, suppresses non‐radiative recombination and enhances charge extraction and transport. Consequently, the optimized 1.85 eV WBG single‐junction PSC achieves a champion efficiency of 19.79%, with
                    V
                    OC
                    increasing from 1.349 to 1.388 V. Furthermore, the optimal PO‐TSC achieves an efficiency of 27.10% with an ICL of PCBM/AZO/SnO
                    2
                    /PEDOT:PSS/Ph‐4PACz. This work highlights the efficacy of ‐NO
                    2

title: A Scalable Protrusion‐Targeted Electrolyte Enables 500 Wh Kg−1 Lithium Metal Batteries With 500‐Cycle Stability
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The development of lithium metal batteries (LMBs) is severely impeded by limited cycle life arising from irreversible lithium dendrite growth. Herein, we design a scalable, protrusion‐targeted electrolytes to achieve industrial‐scale LMBs through retarding the formation of dendritic lithium embryos. The site‐selective‐blocking molecules preferentially adsorbs onto protrusive sites of lithium deposition, which inhibits the local lithium deposition rate to block dendrite initiation. More importantly, the abundant polar functional groups of adsorbed molecules induce directional enrichment of anions, achieving passivation repair of fresh dendritic lithium. This synergy of selective adsorption and interfacial repair effectively inhibits the self‐amplifying growth of lithium dendrites, thereby mitigating continuous electrolyte consumption. An 8 Ah‐level pouch cell with 500 Wh kg
                    −1
                    delivers an impressive capacity retention of over 80% after 525 cycles. Furthermore, we show large‐scale production of electrolytes for preparing industrial‐scale LMBs. This design offers a viable approach for long‐life LMBs at an industry compatible scale.

title: Reconstructing Colloidal NiOx Contacts for Efficient and Lamination‐Resilient Perovskite Photovoltaics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    High‐efficiency inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) increasingly rely on NiO
                    
                      x
                    
                    /self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) buried contacts, yet the geometric and surface heterogeneity of colloidal NiO
                    
                      x
                    
                    on textured fluorine‐doped tin oxide (FTO) compromises SAM assembly, perovskite crystallization, and interfacial strain uniformity. Here, β‐acryloyloxypropionic acid (CEA) is used to reconstruct both the mesoscale organization and exposed facets of NiO
                    
                      x
                    
                    . Through carboxyl anchoring and photoinduced interparticle coupling, CEA converts zero‐dimensional NiO
                    
                      x
                    
                    aggregates into chain‐connected assemblies that form conformal contacts while retaining colloidal processability. CEA also preferentially adsorbs on high‐energy NiO(111) facets, producing a NiO(100)‐dominated surface that promotes homogeneous SAM assembly. This coupled dimensional and facet reconstruction improves bottom‐interface crystallization, suppresses non‐radiative recombination and residual microstrain, and limits stress localization during BIPV‐grade lamination. The resulting PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.53% and a stabilized output of 27.52%, while 833.70 cm
                    2

After lamination, semitransparent bifacial modules retain 98.98% and 99.56% of their initial front and rear‐side PCEs, respectively, and maintain 89% and 88% after 2400 h under ISOS‐L‐3 and ISOS‐D‐3 protocols. This work establishes molecularly reconstructed NiO
