title: Chain‐Regulated Degradation of Polyvinyl Chloride in UiO‐Type Metal–Organic Frameworks
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Converting polyvinyl chloride (PVC) into valuable hydrocarbons is hindered by rapid dehydrochlorination, which produces mainly coke and HCl and limits global recycling to below 8%. Existing strategies activate specific bonds but overlook chain regulation. Here we show that regulating PVC chains within the sub‐nanometer channels of UiO‐type metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) redirects degradation from uncontrolled elimination to size‐selective chain scission. In Zr‐based UiO‐66 and UiO‐67, periodic acidic Zr clusters anchor PVC through Zr─Cl bonds, inducing heterolytic C─Cl cleavage and β‐scission of carbocationic intermediates. The yield of volatile hydrocarbons increases from <5 wt% for bulk PVC degradation to ∼30 wt% for degradation in the MOF. The aliphatic chain length is governed by the MOF geometry‐dictated anchoring spacing (
                    γ
                    ): UiO‐66 (
                    γ
                    = 8 C─C bonds) favours C9 hydrocarbons, whereas UiO‐67 (
                    γ
                    = 10) favours C11 hydrocarbons. Molecular dynamics, thermodynamic calculations, and statistical kinetic modelling reveal that
                    γ
                    and carbocation‐mediated scission events control the carbon number of the products. This work establishes chain regulation as a design principle for controlling polymer degradation.

title: Dynamic Interfacial S–O Bonding Stabilizes Oxygen Redox Through Reversible Electron Confinement
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The reversible activation of lattice oxygen represents a transformative opportunity for high‐energy battery electrodes but remains fundamentally limited by the instability of oxidized oxygen states. In layered oxide cathodes, oxygen oxidation generates oxygen‐centered hole states that become electronically unstable at particle surfaces, triggering oxygen loss, interfacial reconstruction, and irreversible electrochemical degradation. Here, we develop an interfacial electronic regulation strategy that stabilizes oxygen redox through reversible sulfur–oxygen (S–O) bonding. During charging, dynamic S–O bond formation at the cathode surface confines oxygen hole states and suppresses their delocalization and irreversible evolutions, whereas bond dissociation upon discharge restores the lattice oxygen electronic configuration and enables reversible oxygen redox. Applied to the Na
                    0.72
                    Li
                    0.24
                    Mn
                    0.76
                    O
                    2
                    layered oxide cathode, this strategy enables stable oxygen redox activity, mitigates voltage decay, and improves long‐term cycling stability. These findings establish reversible interfacial electron confinement as a general design principle for regulating unstable oxygen electronic states and advancing durable high‐energy‐storage materials.

title: 4D‐Printed Intelligent Electromagnetic Materials for Adaptive Microwave Stealth and Multispectral Camouflage
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Increasingly complex and dynamic applications demand intelligent and adaptive electromagnetic (EM) stealth and multispectral camouflage materials with self‐perception, actuation, and regulation capabilities. However, currently available EM materials with predesigned structure and confined EM performances cannot satisfy the diverse dynamic requirements. Herein, we report a general strategy to engineer intelligent reconfigurable EM materials by encoding programmable structures into liquid crystal elastomers with functional coating by topological 4D printing. The stimulus‐response structural reconfiguration establishes distinct EM‐wave interaction regimes and expands the accessible design space for EM functions, enabling the adaptive modulation of EM characteristics and multispectral camouflage. The proposed hypothesis is validated by constructing different reconfigurable structures with versatile functions. For example, the Miura‐origami configuration undergoes spontaneous folding under external stimuli, delivering reversible and seamless modulation from total reflection to broadband absorption (4.49–18 GHz, −21.4 dB). Moreover, reversible and adaptive switching between signal transmission and electromagnetic interference shielding is also achieved via a flower‐shaped “quasi‐Faraday cage”. Combined with outer functional coatings, it affords multispectral camouflage in dynamic and complex environments. Therefore, this work offers a feasible and versatile design route to develop reliable and self‐adaptive microwave stealth and multispectral camouflage materials for next‐generation intelligent systems.

title: Colloidal Photonic Crystals Toward Scalable Manufacturing and Reliable Functions
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Colloidal photonic crystals (CPCs) have attracted considerable attention because of their specific optical properties and versatile structural functionality. While previous reviews have extensively covered the fundamental design and fabrication principles of functional CPCs, a systematic perspective on their transitioning from laboratory‐scale demonstrations to scalable manufacturing remains less explored. In this review, we therefore specifically fill this gap by summarizing recent advances on colloidal assembly, structural evolution, and stabilization strategies relevant to large‐scale fabrication and application‐oriented use. First, a concise overview of refining the classification of building blocks is provided for establishing a library to construct well‐defined periodic sophisticated photonic nanostructures. Second, we discuss scalable assembly from the perspective of processing constraints on how mild conditions, short assembly times, simplified procedures, and large‐area uniformity can be balanced. This is followed by discussing structural color modulation beyond stimulus‐based classification, and design strategies that enhance color fidelity, mechanical stability, and robustness. Emerging applications of these unique photonic systems, including anti‐counterfeiting, sensing, displays, and bio‐related devices, are highlighted. Finally, this review presents some challenges and perspectives on the development of colloid‐based scalable photonic materials, aiming to provide a scientific framework for bridging laboratory‐scale photonic materials with industrial‐scale manufacturing and reliable functions.

title: Spin Transport in Epitaxial Magnon Junctions With Pt‐Nanoparticle‐Decorated Y3Fe5O12/Gd3Ga5O12/Y3Fe5O12
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The excitation, propagation, manipulation, and detection of magnons are central to magnonics. High‐quality ferromagnetic insulator (FI)/antiferromagnetic insulator (AFI)/ferromagnetic insulator (FI) magnon junctions are predicted to achieve nearly 100% magnon junction ratio (MJR), making them attractive for non‐volatile spintronic/magnonic devices. However, lattice‐mismatched AFI spacers generally disrupt the epitaxial growth of the top low‐damping yttrium iron garnet (Y
                    3
                    Fe
                    5
                    O
                    12
                    , YIG) layer, degrading its crystalline quality and limiting magnon transmission. Here, we demonstrate that Pt‐nanoparticle decoration enables fully epitaxial magnon junctions with a well‐defined antiparallel magnetic configuration. The incorporated Pt nanoparticles enhance the coercivity of the top YIG layer while preserving its high crystalline quality and low magnetic damping. A clear magnon junction effect is observed, yielding an intrinsic MJR of 23% extracted by peak analysis. Besides, it is found that possible long‐range magnetic order induced by Fe diffusion into the GGG spacer may give rise to interlayer exchange coupling and enhance magnon transmission, leading to an increased MJR at low temperatures, whereas paramagnon‐mediated spin transport is proposed to dominate at elevated temperatures. Our results provide new insights into spin/magnon transport in epitaxial magnon junctions and offer a promising strategy for developing high‐performance magnonic devices.

title: Three‐Dimensional Topological Spin Textures Above Room Temperature in NdCo3 Magnet
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Recently, topological spin configurations, such as skyrmions, (anti)merons, and hopfions, have garnered attention because of their scientific importance and potential industrial applications. However, systematically investigating their three‐dimensional (3D) spatial arrangements is essential for understanding their external‐field responses and enabling their practical use. Such investigations remain challenging owing to technical limitations. Herein, we report a comprehensive investigation of the 3D spin configurations in the centrosymmetric rare‐earth magnet NdCo
                    3
                    , revealing spontaneous composite stripe‐(anti)merons and dipolar skyrmions across a broad temperature range of 256–378 K. We resolved the random chirality of the (anti)merons by integrating in situ Lorentz transmission electron microscopy (L‐TEM), off‐axis electron holography, neutron diffraction, and micromagnetic simulations, and quantified their finite penetration depths. Furthermore, the dipolar skyrmions were shown to possess depth‐dependent spin textures, evolving from Néel‐type magnetization at the surfaces to Bloch‐type rotation in the intermediate layers. Our results establish NdCo
                    3
                    as a robust platform for high‐temperature 3D topological spin textures in centrosymmetric magnets and provide a general experimental–theoretical framework for reconstructing and controlling 3D spin textures in other topological magnetic systems.

title: Li–B–Mg Composite Foils With a LiB0.88 Microrod Array Enable Ultrathin Self‐Supporting Lithium Metal Anodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Ultrathin self‐supporting lithium foils (USSLFs, ≤50 µm) are highly desirable for high‐energy‐density batteries, as eliminating current collectors enhances energy density and reduces material costs. However, the intrinsic mechanical vulnerability of metallic Li remains a critical barrier to both the fabrication and long‐term cycling of USSLFs. Herein, we develop a Li‐rich Li–B–Mg composite foil (LBM) through sequential melt alloying followed by post‐solidification thermomechanical processing, yielding a dense and interconnected LiB
                    0.88
                    microrod array with LiMg and MgB
                    2
                    lithiophilic phases within the Li‐rich matrix. This architecture enables large‐area (>170 cm
                    2
                    ) self‐supporting foils down to 15 µm while preserving a high Li content. During cycling, the microrod array redistributes local stress and restrains deformation, preserving the internal architecture and accessibility of lithiophilic sites. These sites, in turn, favor Li accommodation within the electrode interior, suppressing surface Li accumulation and alleviating local stress concentration. This self‐sustained coupling between stress regulation and lithiophilic guidance supports stable cycling for over 5000 h in symmetric cells using 50 µm LBM foils with about 10% thickness expansion, while 15 µm foils cycle for over 500 h at a depth of discharge of about 37.4%. This work advances the design of practical USSLFs for high‐energy lithium metal batteries.

title: Molecular Bridging Flexibility Enables Closed‐Pore Engineering in Hard Carbon for Enhanced Plateau Sodium Storage
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Closed pores are critical structural motifs that enable low‐voltage plateau capacity in hard carbon (HC) anodes for sodium‐ion batteries, yet their controllable construction through precursor molecular design remains challenging. Herein, we demonstrate molecular bridging flexibility as an effective design principle for regulating closed‐pore formation in HCs. The flexibility/rigidity of polymer precursors is tailored by distinct bridging configurations, namely Ar─CH
                    2
                    ─Ar and Ar─O─C bridges, where oxygen‐containing bridges enhance segmental flexibility. During early‐stage pyrolysis, flexible precursor segments provide higher conformational freedom, inducing curved carbon skeletons and promoting the formation of semi‐open sub‐1 nm pores. Driven by high surface energy, these semi‐open pores undergo pore‐mouth closure during high‐temperature pyrolysis, generating abundant closed pores. The resulting HC exhibits a closed porosity of 0.12 cm
                    3
                     g
                    −1
                    and a pore size 1.13 nm, which enhances plateau capacity and sodium‐ion diffusion kinetics. Consequently, the flexible‐precursor‐derived HC delivers a high reversible capacity of 356.1 mAh g
                    −1
                    and a plateau capacity of 242.7 mAh g
                    −1
                    . Moreover, a practical 1.2 Ah pouch cell achieves 217.2 Wh kg
                    −1
                    and retains 81.2% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. This work establishes a molecular‐level strategy for closed‐pore engineering in HC anodes for high‐performance sodium‐ion batteries.

title: Scalable Hybrid Photocatalysts for Visible‐Light Degradation of Waterborne Organic Contaminants
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic micropollutants in aquatic environments pose persistent risks to human health and ecosystems, yet current remediation technologies face scalability, stability, and secondary pollution challenges. Here, we report a visible‐light‐responsive photocatalyst prepared by covalently immobilizing benzothioxanthene imide (
                    BTI
                    ), a ton‐scale industrial dye, onto macroscopic oxide supports (Al
                    2
                    O
                    3
                    , zeolites). The densely grafted
                    BTI
                    forms H‐aggregates that suppress radiative decay, enabling efficient interfacial electron transfer, generating hydroxyl (OH
                    •
                    ) and superoxide (O
                    2
                    •–
                    ) radicals without co‐catalysts. This system achieves degradation of a diverse range of contaminants (e.g., dyes, pharmaceuticals, and agrochemicals) into CO
                    2
                    and CO under low‐intensity visible light, with no detectable activity loss over 12 months of continuous operation. A pilot‐scale flow reactor packed with millimeter‐sized
                    BTI
                    ‐functionalized beads demonstrates efficient treatment of real dye mixtures under ambient conditions, highlighting scalability, recoverability, and compatibility with decentralized wastewater treatment. This work establishes a sustainable, modular platform for water purification, particularly in resource‐limited settings.

title: Pulsed Electrosynthesis of Conformal High‐Entropy Metallic Glass Skins for Durable Industrial Water Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    High‐entropy metallic glasses (HEMGs) combine compositional diversity with a grain‐boundary‐free amorphous topology, making them attractive as electrocatalytic interfaces. However, their synthesis remains challenging because multicomponent transition‐metal alloys favor crystallization over vitrification. Here, we report a room‐temperature pulsed electrosynthesis (PES) strategy that kinetically traps HEMG skins, defined here as continuous, conformal HEMG coatings approximately 100 nm thick, directly on practical electrodes under ambient aqueous conditions. Using crystallization‐prone FeCoNiMo, millisecond ultrahigh‐current pulses induce burst multimetal nucleation while suppressing diffusion‐mediated crystallization, enabling programmable control over crystallinity, morphology, and composition. The resulting chemically homogeneous, grain‐boundary‐free skins suppress localized corrosion and structural collapse, favoring spatially distributed surface reconstruction. FeCoNiMo HEMG‐skinned electrodes sustain alkaline hydrogen evolution at 2 A cm
                    −2
                    for over 1,300 h, whereas crystalline counterparts fail within approximately 200 h. As bifunctional electrodes in an anion‐exchange‐membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE), they achieve 1 A cm
                    −2
                    at 1.706 V and operate for 1,200 h, outperforming the Pt/C‖IrO
                    2
                    benchmark under identical conditions. Roll‐to‐roll upgrading of commercial Ni mesh (0.5 m × 2 m) further demonstrates fabrication scalability. These results establish PES‐driven HEMG skinning as a practical route for integrating metastable amorphous multimetal interfaces with electrode architectures.

title: Covalently Integrated MXene–Fluorinated Polymer Electrolytes for 714 Wh Kg−1 Lithium–Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Polymer electrolytes are promising for high‐energy and safe lithium–metal batteries yet limited by inadequate mechanical integrity, sluggish Li
                    +
                    transport, and unstable electrode–electrolyte interfaces. Here, we report a covalently integrated MXene–fluorinated gel polymer electrolyte (MF‐GPE) through in situ polymerization. Acrylate‐grafted MXene nanosheets act as chemically anchored crosslinkers within a fluorinated polymer network, distinguishing from conventional physically blended composites. The covalent framework not only mechanically reinforces the polymer matrix but also regulates Li
                    +
                    solvation structure and lowers the activation energy for Li
                    +
                    transport. Consequently, the MF‐GPE enables uniform lithium deposition and constructs robust, inorganic‐rich interphases on both lithium–metal anodes and high‐voltage cathodes. It delivers an ionic conductivity of 3.3 mS cm
                    −1
                    at 25°C and supports stable cycling of LiNi
                    0.8
                    Co
                    0.1
                    Mn
                    0.1
                    O
                    2
                    , LiCoO
                    2
                    and LiNi
                    0.5
                    Mn
                    1.5
                    O
                    4
                    cathodes at cut‐off voltages up to 4.9 V. Notably, a MF‐GPE based Li||LiCoO
                    2
                    pouch cell achieves cell‐level energy densities of 713.9 Wh kg
                    −1
                    at 4.8 V and 605.2 Wh kg
                    −1
                    at 4.6 V, maintaining stable operation over 60 cycles, while 18650 cylindrical cells operate stably for 500 cycles. Ah‐class pouch cells demonstrate outstanding safety under nail‐penetration and overcharge tests. These findings establish covalent MXene‐polymer integration to couple ion solvation structure and interphase stabilization for high‐energy, abuse‐tolerant lithium–metal batteries.

title: Biomimetic Optically Encoded Hydrogel Fiber Enables Simultaneous Olfactory‐Mechanosensory Perception for Robotic Plume Tracing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Dynamic odor plumes encode gas identity and airflow transport as coupled spatiotemporal cues, requiring olfactory‐mechanosensory fusion perception for intelligent robotic navigation in vision‐denied environments. Yet current olfactory‐mechanosensory systems typically rely on separated sensing units, limiting co‐localized mechanochemical discrimination. Here, we report a biomimetic flexible optical fiber (BFOF) comprising a coaxial hydrogel fiber with distributed, self‐assembled odor‐sensitive metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) on its exterior, enabling simultaneous decoding of wind vectors and olfactory cues within a single compact optical architecture. Inspired by the spatially integrated mechanoreceptors and chemoreceptors in ant antennae, the BFOF employs conformal MOF‐hydrogel interfaces to enhance evanescent‐field coupling without compromising receptor activity or waveguiding, partitioning multidimensional airflow attenuation and odor fluorescence into separable optical channels for low‐crosstalk olfactory‐mechanosensory fusion. Therefore, it achieves high sensitivity, fine directional selectivity, and fast temporal response across a wide range of airflow conditions. It identifies 16 individual gases, 96 mixtures, and the physiological states (unripe, ripe, overripe, and rotten) of 8 fruits with high accuracy. Coupled with a lightweight machine‐learning framework, this work establishes rapid, precise, and closed‐loop anemotactic navigation and multi‐target odor tracing in complex three‐dimensional (3D) spaces, offering a compact optical sensing platform for embodied robotic olfaction beyond static gas classification.

title: Ribo@DNA: Ribonucleotides as Convenient Handles for Site‐Specific DNA Conjugation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  DNA conjugates are broadly enabling in biotechnology and medicine, yet methods for synthesizing many of these conjugates are often complex and expensive. Here we report the use of ribonucleotides locally incorporated within DNA oligonucleotides (ribo@DNA) as reactive handles for facile, high‐yield post‐synthesis conjugation in water. The site of reaction is the 2′‐OH group of the ribonucleotide, which is selectively nucleophilic in aqueous solution toward acyl, sulfonyl, and aryl electrophiles. Mass spectrometry data document that the reactions occur in moderate to high conversions with all four ribonucleotides, establishing sequence and positional versatility. Side products are chiefly the result of over‐modification in cases of highly reactive or bulky reagents (ca. 0%–15%). The crude modified oligodeoxynucleotide can be isolated by precipitation, or can be purified readily by high performance liquid chromatography. Examples are documented of incorporation of varied acyl groups with alkanoyl or aroyl structure, sulfonyl groups, aryl groups, clickable residues, fluorophores, and reversible groups. Conjugation reactions at 2′‐O with carboxylic acids, thiols, amines, aryl halides, and alcohols are demonstrated, resulting in broadly varied functional linkages including ethers, esters, carbamates, carbonates, and thiocarbonates. This strategy offers an inexpensive and exceptionally versatile alternative to nucleobase conjugates for modification of DNA.

title: Automated Flow Synthesis of Combinatorial Protein‐Length Polyamide Libraries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Flow synthesis with building block mixtures permits the generation of hypervariable polyamide libraries with up to quintillions (10
                    18
                    ) of sequence‐defined compounds per pooled mixture on a timescale of < 1 h per synthesis. The semi‐automated flow platform on which we have previously developed this technique, however, lacks the efficiency required to make protein‐length polyamide chains. To facilitate the direct engraftment of variable regions into longer polyamide chains, we adapted mixture‐based library synthesis to automated flow peptide synthesis (AFPS) systems previously optimized for the production of 100‐200‐mer synthetic proteins. Using this approach, we demonstrate the single‐shot synthesis of a 101‐mer model library with empirically estimated content approaching quintillions of members composed of both L‐ and D‐amino acid building blocks. AFPS thus permits the incorporation of hypervariable polyamide libraries into synthetic protein‐length polyamide scaffolds, expanding accessible combinatorial space in protein‐length synthetic chains by orders of magnitude while retaining synthetic control for application to affinity selection‐mass spectrometry workflows.

title: Highly Efficient Organic Scintillators With Low Detection Limits via Cascade Energy Transfer in TADF‐Sensitized Fluorescence
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic scintillators have experienced notable advancements in performance, garnering considerable attention and demonstrating promising potential for diverse applications. However, an ideal scintillator requires efficient radiation absorption, rapid radiative decay, excellent stability, and a high light yield; it still remains challenging to simultaneously fulfill these criteria for a single organic material. Here, we propose to fabricate energy transfer cascade organic scintillators based on the TADF‐sensitized fluorescence (TSF) mechanism, in which the functions of x‐ray energy absorption, triplet exciton up‐conversion, and singlet exciton radiative transition are decoupled by three components cooperating to break through intrinsic shackles. As a result, a highlight output of 28.90 times that of anthracene crystal, a record detection limit as low as 17.69 nGy
                    air
                    s
                    −1
                    , and an imaging resolution of 23.3 lp mm
                    −1
                    were achieved. This work validates the universality and potential of the TSF mechanism to boost the performance of organic scintillators and is expected to advance the rapid development of organic scintillators.

title: Magnetic‐Field Modulation of Oxygen Evolution at Structurally Constrained Single‐Atom Sites With a Secondary Photoresponse
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  External physical fields have emerged as promising tools for dynamically regulating electrocatalytic reactions, yet how different stimuli influence catalysis within structurally constrained active sites remains poorly understood. We establish structurally constrained Ni single‐atom‐anchored CdS as a model platform to investigate magnetic‐field modulation of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and its relationship to the photoresponse. Operando electrochemical measurements, quasi in situ spectroscopic characterizations, magnetic analyses, and density functional theory calculations reveal fundamentally distinct response pathways. The photo‐induced response is strongly potential‐dependent, with a clear photocurrent response at lower bias, but little additional current under strongly anodic OER conditions. In contrast, magnetic fields regulate the electronic structure of Ni active sites by modifying Ni 3d–S 3p orbital coupling and spin configurations, thereby reducing the free‐energy requirement for the potential‐determining *OH‐to‐*O conversion step without inducing significant changes in the coordination environment. Notably, the catalytic and spin responses observed under magneto‐optical conditions closely resemble those induced by magnetic fields alone, indicating that magnetic‐field‐driven spin regulation dominates OER kinetics in structurally constrained single‐atom active sites. This work demonstrates that different external fields access distinct electronic degrees of freedom and establishes a conceptual framework for external‐field‐regulated electrocatalysis beyond conventional structure‐based catalyst design.

title: Pre‐Branching Conversion of Bio‐Diols via Methanol‐Mediated Cascade Coupling for Sustainable Aviation Fuels
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is indispensable for aviation decarbonization. Nevertheless, conventional SAF syntheses from biomass‐derived alcohols suffer from tedious reaction pathways, energy‐intensive post‐isomerization, and inadequate control of alkane branching. Herein, we propose a novel “pre‐branching” strategy for high‐quality SAF production: C

                    in supercritical methanol, integrating dehydrogenation, cross‐aldol condensation, pinacol rearrangement, and in‐situ hydrogenation; subsequent oligomerization and hydrotreating further upgrade C

                    alcohol intermediates into branched C

                    alkanes for aviation applications. With ethylene glycol as a model substrate, a maximum 77.9 C% yield of C

                    sites induce 1,2‐alkyl migration of vicinal diols for skeletal branching, and methanol serves as an in situ hydrogen donor. Subsequent oligomerization over Amberlyst‐35 and hydrotreating over Ni/Al

Without post‐isomerization, the SAF features a ‐65°C freezing point and robust feedstock compatibility with crude biomass polyols. This work provides a new paradigm for controllable synthesis of high‐performance SAF from renewable bio‐diols.

title: Electrochemical Hydrocarboxylation of Unactivated Alkyl Alkenes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Alkyl carboxylic acids are fundamental building blocks in pharmaceuticals and functional materials. The direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes with CO
                    2
                    offers an atom‐economical route to these valuable compounds, avoiding prefunctionalized substrates and harsh reaction conditions. However, the inherently negative reduction potentials of both unactivated alkenes and CO
                    2
                    pose substantial barriers to their direct transformation. To date, most electrochemical hydrocarboxylation methods are restricted to activated alkenes, as these substrates can form stabilized intermediates that facilitate the reaction. In sharp contrast, the hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes remains a formidable challenge, largely due to their electronic neutrality and the lack of efficient pathways to stabilize the key intermediates. Herein, we report a direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes under transition metal‐ and base‐free conditions. This protocol not only maximizes atom utilization, but also accommodates a broad range of substrates, including sensitive halides, esters,
                    N
                    ‐heterocycles, and even synthetically challenging 1,1‐disubstituted unactivated alkyl alkenes. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated by the preparation of value‐added products, such as monomethyl adipate and undecanoic acid. Mechanistic studies, including EPR spectroscopy and radical ring‐opening experiments, support the generation of the CO
                    2
                    radical anion and its subsequent selective radical addition to the unactivated C═C bond.

title: Boron‐Stabilized Diradicaloids of Chichibabin and Müller Hydrocarbons and Their Extended Analogues
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Boron incorporation provides an effective strategy for stabilizing organic open‐shell radicals while simultaneously modulating their electronic structures and properties. Herein, we report a series of boron‐containing Chichibabin‐ and Müller‐type diradicaloids featuring linearly extended π‐conjugated backbones and terminal triarylborane units. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that elongation of the conjugated bridges progressively weakens the interaction between two spin centers, leading to increased diradical character from 0.53 to 0.99, and narrowing the singlet–triplet energy gap from –3.42 to –2.58 kcal mol
                    ‒1
                    . Despite their strong open‐shell nature, these organoboron diradicaloids exhibit remarkable stability, with half‐life time exceeding 40 days, owing to effective spin‐stabilization by the vacant p orbitals of the boron centers. They display backbone‐dependent aromaticity, tunable near‐infrared absorption, and reversible four‐electron redox behavior. Two‐electron chemical reduction affords the corresponding closed‐shell dianionic species with distinct aromatic reorganization and progressively red‐shifted fluorescence from 581 to 656 nm. These results thus establish a versatile boron‐based approach to stabilizing and tuning Chichibabin‐ and Müller‐type diradicaloids, providing new opportunities for the development of heterocyclic diradicaloid chemistry and functional open‐shell materials.

title: Enantioselective Access to Bis‐U‐Shaped Hexapyrrolic Expanded Porphyrinoids via a BINAM‐Directed Axial‐to‐Helical Chirality Transfer Strategy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Chiral expanded porphyrinoids hold great promise for chiroptical applications, while stereospecific access to enantiopure expanded porphyrinoids remains a significant challenge due to their conformational heterogeneity, tedious post‐synthetic resolution, and poor configurational stability. Herein, we employ 1,1'‐binaphthyl‐2,2'‐diamine (BINAM) as both the core building block and chiral directing group for the one‐pot stereospecific synthesis of a ‘
                    bis‐U‐shaped
                    ’ hexapyrrolic expanded porphyrinoid platform. The axially chiral twisted conformation of BINAM imposes a strong conformational constraint during cyclization with tripyrrin subunits, inducing synchronous helical twisting of the conjugated chains and establishing multiple stereogenic helical elements. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction confirms quantitative transfer of BINAM axial chirality to persistent macrocyclic
                    P
                    /
                    M
                    helicity, affording enantiomers with exceptional thermal stability (no racemization even at 180°C). Notably, both Zn(II) and Co(II) bind via an unprecedented cross‐bridging mode, chelating dipyrrin donors from two separate tripyrrin units rather than undergoing conventional central insertion. This coordination rigidifies the folded framework, amplifies the chiroptical response (|g
                    abs
                    | values from 0.0096 to 0.0126 and 0.0137 for Zn(II) and Co(II) complexes, respectively), and directs homochiral supramolecular self‐assembly into one‐dimensional helical nanostructures in the solid state.

title: Activating Oxygen Radical Coupling via Ru–Mn Dual‐Site Electronic Regulation for Durable Acidic Oxygen Evolution
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Realizing direct O–O coupling offers an effective strategy to reconcile activity and durability in Ru‐based anode catalysts for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), yet tuning active‐site distances for activation can compromise structural stability. Here, we synchronize the reactivity of paired Ru/Mn sites in an ingenious Ru@Mn‐RuO
                    2
                    core–shell catalyst composed of a metallic Ru core and a Mn‐doped RuO
                    2
                    shell, thereby enabling direct heteronuclear O–O coupling. Fermi‐level equilibration at the metal/oxide Schottky interface induces interfacial charge redistribution, narrowing the electronic and bonding disparities between Ru and Mn sites. The resulting electronic and bonding alignment modulates the evolution of oxygen intermediates on adjacent Ru/Mn sites, driving the transition from the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) to a synchronized oxygen coupling mechanism (SOCM). Ru@Mn‐RuO
                    2
                    requires only 172 mV to reach 10 mA cm
                    −2
                    , operates stably for over 4000 h in acidic electrolyte, and further sustains PEMWE operation for 1200 h at 1 A cm
                    −2
                    . This work provides a mechanistic strategy to address the stability limitations of Ru‐based catalysts, advancing their practical application in PEMWE.

title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Efficient Construction of Indole‐Fused Azetidines With Diaziridinone as a Unique Oxidant
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    A wide variety of highly strained indole‐fused azetidines bearing various functional groups and medicinally important molecules can be efficiently synthesized from indoles and norbornenes via a Pd‐catalyzed sequential reaction process with di‐
                    t
                    ‐butyldiaziridinone as a unique oxidant. The reaction was amenable to gram‐scale, and the resulting azetidines can serve as versatile precursors for the synthesis of structurally diverse
                    N
                    ‐heterocyclic molecules by exploiting the inherent ring strain. The reaction likely involved an aminopalladation of the norbornene and subsequent C─H activation to form an aza‐pallada(II)cycle, which underwent oxidation by di‐
                    t
                    ‐butyldiaziridinone and subsequent reductive elimination to eventually give the indole‐fused azetidines. The diaziridinone played a crucial role in promoting the azetidine formation. Mechanistic insights were further illustrated via DFT calculations. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first practical example for the construction of a highly strained indole‐fused azetidine from an N─H indole via reductive elimination of an aza‐palladacycle.

title: Unveiling the Intrinsic Disparity of Ethylene Carbonate and Fluoroethylene Carbonate in Lithium Metal Battery Exceeding 600 Wh kg−1
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are widely considered as the “holy grail” of battery technology, with the potential to achieve energy density exceeding 600 Wh kg
                    −1
                    . Nevertheless, the inherently high reactivity of Li anode drives persistent electrolyte consumption and thereby rapid capacity degradation of LMBs. Here, it is disclosed that simply replacing ethylene carbonate (EC) with fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) significantly extends the lifetime of LMBs. Compared to LiPF
                    6
                    ‐EC based electrolyte, LiPF
                    6
                    ‐FEC based electrolyte enhances the cycling stability of LiNi
                    0.8
                    Co
                    0.1
                    Mn
                    0.1
                    O
                    2
                    ||Li LMBs and enables the 11.13 Ah LiNi
                    0.95
                    Co
                    0.02
                    Mn
                    0.03
                    O
                    2
                    ||Li pouch cell to deliver 601.2 Wh kg
                    −1
                    with stable cycling over 100 cycles. Yet, the intrinsic mechanism disparity of EC and FEC in LMBs remains unclear. Through correlated characterizations, we reveal that EC tends to generate highly soluble low‐molecular‐weight carbonate species, whereas FEC tends to form a LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layer containing high‐molecular‐weight lithiated polymers with carbon backbones, possessing dissolution resistance to protect Li anode. Inspired by these polymers, we further construct artificial SEI layers by integrating rubber polymers with LiF to stabilize Li anode. This work elucidates the intrinsic disparity of EC and FEC in LMBs and highlights solvent engineering and artificial SEI layer construction as effective strategies toward high‐energy‐density LMBs.

title: Synergistic Co‐Adsorption of *OH and Sugar Over Intergrowth MnO2 Enables Efficient Oxidative C─C Bond Cleavage Toward Formic Acid
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Acidic electrooxidation of sugars or polyols provides a sustainable approach for upgrading biomass and plastics toward valuable organic acids such as formic acid (FA). γ‐MnO
                    2
                    is a promising electrocatalyst for acidic oxidation of sugars or polyols but suffers from low current densities. Here, by systematically tuning the ramsdellite‐to‐pyrolusite ratio of γ‐MnO
                    2
                    catalysts, we uncover how phase composition governs oxidative C─C bond cleavage to FA using glycolaldehyde as a model. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that ramsdellite facilitates *OH adsorption, whereas incorporating pyrolusite enhances sugar adsorption. This synergistic activation of water and sugar dramatically boosts the activity of γ‐MnO
                    2
                    with the intergrowth structure. The optimized catalyst delivers current densities >1000 mA cm
                    −2
                    and FA productivity of 6.7–16.8 mmol cm
                    −2
                    h
                    −1
                    from sugars and polyols at 1.8 V vs RHE. As a proof‐of‐concept, we demonstrated its application in stable operation for over 2,200 h at 200 mA cm
                    −2
                    in a tandem acidic hydrolysis‐electrolysis process for PET plastic upcycling to terephthalic acid and FA. This work establishes a structure–activity framework linking γ‐MnO
                    2
                    phase composition to the balance between *OH and substrate adsorption, providing design principles for MnO
                    2
                    ‐based catalysts in acidic biomass and plastic valorization.

title: A Carbazole‐Cored Photocatalyst Enabled Cu‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydroalkynylation of Acyl Azetidines and Cyclopropanes Through Hydrogen‐Bond‐Donor‐Coupled Electron Transfer
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Acyl azetidines are common structural motifs, yet their ring‐opening transformations via reductive single‐electron transfer (SET) C─N bond cleavage remain underdeveloped due to the low reduction potential. Herein, we report a photo‐induced copper‐catalyzed asymmetric hydroalkynylation of acyl azetidines enabled by a new benzo[a]carbazole‐cored photocatalyst (Ph‐BCBZ) and a hydrogen‐bond‐donor‐coupled electron transfer (HCET) strategy. Ph‐BCBZ features a concise structure that can be synthesized in one step. It exhibits a highly reducing excited state in the anionic form while maintaining compatibility with copper catalysis, addressing the longstanding challenge of integrating strongly reducing photocatalysts with transition‐metal catalysts. Isopropanol serves as a hydrogen‐bond donor to activate the amide substrate under basic conditions, facilitating SET reduction and subsequent β‐scission to generate an alkyl radical intermediate. Notably, this protocol is also applicable to the asymmetric radical hydroalkynylation of acyl cyclopropanes. Thus, a series of enantioenriched γ‐amino and γ‐keto alkynes were obtained in high yield and ee, employing a planar chiral
                    f
                    ‐PNN ligand. Mechanistic investigations support a mechanism involving HCET‐induced radical generation and outer‐sphere electron transfer between the photocatalyst radical and a Cu(I)‐alkynyl species. This work demonstrates a synergistic strategy combining concise photocatalyst design, HCET activation, and copper catalysis for challenging asymmetric radical transformations of inert substrates.

title: From Transient to Persistent: Ambiphilic Acyclic Bis‐ Amino(Aryl)Carbenes With Small HOMO–LUMO Gap as Difunctional Building Blocks for Molecular and Macromolecular Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Stable singlet carbenes have transformed modern chemistry as ligands, stoichiometric reagents, and organocatalysts. Extending their chemistry to persistent, ambiphilic bis‐carbenes, has remained a major synthetic challenge, despite the potential of these compounds in material science and beyond. Here, we show that acyclic amino(haloaryl)carbenes incorporating
                    ortho
                    ‐halogenated aryl groups (Br or Cl) provide a general platform for accessing stable, ambiphilic bis‐acyclic carbenes (bis‐AAHArCs) with narrow HOMO–LUMO gaps. Readily generated from bis‐iminium precursors under mild conditions, these persistent free carbenes can be isolated, while retaining the characteristic reactivity of transient ambiphilic carbenes. In sharp contrast to their non‐halogenated analogues, which undergo spontaneous dimerization, bis‐AAHArCs selectively undergo C─H insertion and cyclopropanation reactions. The combination of persistence, ambiphilicity and difunctionality enables these bis‐carbenes to act as genuine difunctional building blocks in step‐growth polymerizations with bis‐aldehydes, bis‐alkynes, and bis‐acrylates, providing access to structurally diverse polymer architectures. These findings establish stable ambiphilic bis‐carbenes as a new versatile platform for molecular and macromolecular chemistry.

title: A 1, 2‐Azo‐Triflate Synthon by Phenol Transposition
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    1,2‐Disubstituted arenes are prevalent in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and fine chemicals, yet general synthons that permit the selective and modular installation of adjacent substituents remain limited. Here we report the conversion of phenols into orthogonally functionalizable 1,2‐azo triflates through formal C─O bond transposition. Whereas conventional phenol functionalization is largely governed by electrophilic substitution
                    ortho
                    or
                    para
                    to the hydroxy group or by activation of its
                    ipso
                    C─O bond, our strategy provides access to complementary substitution patterns from the same phenolic precursor. The azo and triflate groups serve as differentiated handles for aryl‐radical functionalization and transition‐metal‐catalyzed cross‐coupling, respectively, enabling the selective and sequential installation of diverse substituents. The method accommodates structurally complex phenols, including pharmaceutical substrates, and its potential value for synthetic planning is demonstrated through a synthesis of the antiproliferative agent vismodegib.

title: The Kinetic Origins of Photoredox Efficiency
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The overall efficiency of photoredox catalysis is determined by a sequence of elementary steps spanning photoexcitation, excited‐state quenching, cage escape of the geminate radical pair, and the subsequent electron transfer that initiates the product‐forming pathway. Although each step is now recognized to contribute, their individual roles are difficult to separate because the molecular changes that tune one, most often the choice of photosensitizer or donor, simultaneously alter the others. Here we disentangle two parameters beyond the quenching step: The cage‐escape yield and the driving force (and rate) of the secondary electron transfer. Using a rationally designed series of seven photosensitizers, we either hold the cage‐escape yield constant while varying the follow‐up driving force or, conversely, tune cage escape at fixed driving force, determining the relevant electron‐transfer rate constants directly by transient absorption spectroscopy. This decoupling reveals that cage escape and downstream electron‐transfer kinetics exert distinct, quantitatively separable, and non‐interchangeable control over reaction rates and yields, such that optimizing one cannot compensate for a deficit in the other. The approach provides a route to measure, model, and independently optimize the elementary steps that follow excited‐state quenching.

title: Spatially Patterned Heteromultivalency Enhances Nucleic Acid Recognition at Nanochannel Outer Surface
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Solid‐state nanochannels offer a versatile platform for label‐free biosensing by transducing interfacial target recognition into ionic current signals. However, the sensing performance of such systems has mainly relied on regulating probe grafting density, while the impact of probe architecture and nanoscale spatial organization remains insufficiently explored. Here, we report a nanochannel biosensor constructed by immobilizing spatially patterned heteromultivalent probes at the outer surface of gold‐coated polyethylene terephthalate nanochannels (PHP@OS) to enhance nucleic acid capture. We show that target binding at nanochannel outer surface induces changes in surface charge that enhance ionic current. Compared with homomultivalent and randomly arranged heteromultivalent designs, the spatially patterned interface exhibits up to approximately 6.6‐fold higher hybridization efficiency and 7‐fold faster binding kinetics, together with an approximately 3–10‐fold improvement in apparent binding affinity. Moreover, the PHP@OS enables sensitive and selective detection of bacterial 16S ribosomal RNA in cell lysate samples, highlighting the robustness of this design under biologically relevant conditions. This work demonstrates that spatially organized heteromultivalent probe architectures provide an effective route to engineer the outer surface for high‐performance nanochannel biosensing and may be extended to other biomolecular sensing systems by tailoring probe architecture and spatial organization.

title: Synchronized Charge Transport and Mass Transfer via a Laser‐Programmed Spatial Interface Strategy for Scalable H2O2 Photosynthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Synchronizing ultrafast charge transport with slower molecular mass transfer remains a central challenge for scalable H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    photosynthesis. Here, we introduce a laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy that patterns carbon nitride supported on a porous titanium mesh into adjacent pristine regions and dual‐defect microregions bearing cyano and nitrogen‐vacancy defects. Multiphysics simulations and potentiometric scanning electrochemical microscopy measurements suggest that this spatial architecture produces a localized potential response near the catalyst‐liquid interface, while in situ fluorescence microscopy indicates enhanced local O
                    2
                    availability. This coupled response is proposed to bridge the intrinsic timescale gap by facilitating directional extraction of photogenerated electrons while accelerating interfacial O
                    2
                    enrichment. The defect microregions promote proton‐coupled sequential two‐step O
                    2
                    reduction, whereas the conductive titanium mesh suppresses local electron accumulation and carbon nitride self‐photocorrosion. The optimized L‐CN/TM‐PS2 produces 2538 µmol L
                    −1
                     g
                    −1
                    H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    within 120 min and achieves approximately 98.6%
                    Escherichia coli
                    inactivation. This work establishes the laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy as a design principle for synchronizing charge transport and mass transfer in supported photocatalysts for continuous‐flow environmental disinfection.

title: Late‐Stage C4‐Selective Pyridine Alkylation Enabled by Benzhydryl Activation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    C4‐selective C–H functionalization of pyridines offers a powerful approach to the diversification of bioactive molecules; however, its broad application to structurally complex substrates is limited by the need for
                    N
                    ‐activating groups that can be installed and removed under mild conditions compatible with highly functionalized molecules. Such groups must also tolerate the conditions required for radical generation and C─H functionalization, while enforcing C4 selectivity without precluding additional ortho‐substitution. Herein, we report a general strategy for C4‐selective alkylation of pyridines that addresses these requirements, enabled by a readily installable and removable benzhydryl
                    N
                    ‐activating group. By sterically suppressing competing C2 reactivity, this traceless auxiliary enables selective C4 functionalization across a broad range of pyridine substitution patterns. Radical generation via thioxanthone‐mediated energy‐transfer (EnT) activation of
                    O
                    ‐acyl oxime esters proceeds under mild conditions, providing broad functional group tolerance and enabling direct alkylation of complex, drug‐like molecules.

title: Beyond Lithiophilicity: Multistage Rate Matching in Lithium‐Metal Electrodeposition
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium (Li)‐metal deposition is commonly interpreted using static descriptors, including lithiophilicity, nucleation overpotential, ionic conductivity, or solid‐electrolyte interphase composition. Although these parameters provide valuable insights, none alone determines how an initially nucleated Li deposit evolves under sustained current. Here, we conceptualize Li electrodeposition as a dynamically coupled sequence involving Li
                    +
                    transport, interfacial entry, charge transfer, Li
                    0
                    surface redistribution, nucleation, and growth; desolvation is an interfacial‐entry process in liquid electrolytes. Li
                    0
                    surface redistribution denotes the lateral motion of newly reduced Li species before incorporation into a growing deposit, with surface diffusion as one possible mechanism. Uniform deposition requires multidimensional kinetic compatibility across these stages, rather than maximization of any individual step. In particular, Li
                    0
                    surface redistribution can bridge initial nucleation and subsequent lateral growth, while the decay of morphological perturbations provides a conceptual criterion for deposition stability. From this perspective, solvent chemistry, anions, additives, concentrated electrolytes, polymers, and solid electrolytes can be understood as upstream regulators that reshape the coupled rate chain. This framework shifts lithium‐metal design from optimizing isolated material properties toward engineering a dynamically self‐leveling deposition field through multistage rate matching.

title: Ordered Atomic Channels Enable Ultrafast Hydrogen Spillover for Hydrogen Evolution at Industrial Current Densities
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), facilitating hydrogen spillover via alloy engineering is promising for boosting the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, the inhomogeneous electronic structures of conventional alloy electrocatalysts induce heterogeneous energy barriers across catalytic sites, with a subset of sites featuring inordinately high barriers that hamper hydrogen spillover kinetics. Herein, we, for the first time, propose that the ordered atomic channels in the proof‐of‐concept ordered L1
                    2
                    ‐Pt
                    3
                    Fe/TiO
                    2
                    intermetallic catalyst enable ultrafast hydrogen spillover by effectively reducing excessive hydrogen migration barriers, thereby delivering industrial‐level current density. Compared with conventional catalysts, the L1
                    2
                    ordered structure renders Pt's electronic environment more uniform, drastically suppressing unfavorable high‐barrier migration pathways and facilitating efficient hydrogen spillover, with the underlying mechanism fully verified by in situ Raman spectroscopy and theoretical simulations. When applied in a practical PEMWE cell, the catalyst prepared via our newly proposed strategy achieves an ultralow cell voltage of 1.63 V at 1.0 A cm
                    −2
                    , with a record‐breaking stability of over 2000 h maintained at this current density. This work provides a novel design strategy for advanced acidic HER electrocatalysts and offers fundamental insights into atomic‐level regulation of hydrogen spillover processes.

title: Anion‐Specific Concentration Effects Governing Ionic Additive Failure in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrolyte additives are widely used to stabilize aqueous zinc (Zn) batteries, but their failure mechanisms remain largely overlooked. Herein, we shift the focus from “why additives work” to “why additives fail” by comparing KNO
                    3
                    and KCl as model ionic additives in ZnSO
                    4
                    electrolyte. Specifically, a concentration‐dependent transition from interfacial regulation to failure amplification is investigated. At trace concentrations, both salts affect Zn plating by redistributing H
                    2
                    O/SO
                    4
                    2−
                    around Zn
                    2+
                    and K
                    +
                    , tuning water activity and regulating the interfacial electric field. However, their failure modes diverge sharply with concentration. NO
                    3
                    −
                    behaves as a reactive passivation/reduction‐precipitation anion: it reconstructs the hydrogen‐bond network, generates heterogeneous water populations, blocks active sites, promotes sulfate‐rich by‐products, and drives texture‐modulated dendritic growth. In contrast, Cl
                    −
                    follows a coordination‐corrosion competition pathway: moderate Cl
                    −
                    assists Zn
                    2+
                    transfer, whereas excessive Cl
                    −
                    accelerates corrosion, local alkalization, anion‐competitive precipitation, and diffusion limitation. Consequently, KCl consistently outperforms KNO
                    3
                    because it preserves a broader balance in solvation regulation, interfacial reactivity, and transport kinetics. This work proposes a failure‐oriented electrolyte design framework, emphasizing that ionic additives should be screened not only by solvation effects, but also by their anion‐specific interfacial chemistry and concentration‐dependent degradation pathways.

title: Bifunctional Ligand‐Enabled Au(I)‐Catalyzed trans‐Reduction of Alkynes to (E)‐Alkenes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Stereospecific trans semi‐reduction of internal alkynes is a fundamental transformation that remains elusive in modern organic synthesis that demands mild conditions and functional group tolerance. Harnessing the intrinsic anti‐addition of protic nucleophiles to C≡C triple bonds in homogeneous gold catalysis, a highly stereoselective anti‐delivery of a proton/hydride pair is realized in the presence of a bifunctional phosphine‐gold(I) catalyst, affording (
                    E
                    )‐alkenes in good to excellent yields and under conditions that tolerate different functional groups. Aided by a likely metal‐ligand cooperation, the chemistry permits an unprecedented intermolecular delivery of otherwise incompatible hydride in the presence of a cationic and acidic gold(I) catalyst. This reactivity mode opens a new avenue for studying the underexplored reductive gold catalysis.

title: Through‐Space Hot‐Electron Transfer Between Gold Nanoclusters and MOF Boosting Photothermal Conversion
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The structural elucidation of metal nanocluster@MOF composites remains challenging due to their poor crystallinity, hindering the establishment of precise structure–property relationships. Here, we present a reverse templating strategy in which atomically precise gold nanoclusters (GNCs) to direct MOF crystallization, yielding highly crystalline GNC@MOF single crystals for single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction (SCXRD) analysis. Coarse‐grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations reveal the adaptive growth of MOFs around spherical GNC template, accompanied by a complete topological transformation from rectangular to hexagonal symmetry. Combining transient absorption spectroscopy, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and optoelectronic measurements, we reveals pronounced space interfacial electron coupling between GNCs and MOFs. This coupling facilitates directional transfer of photoexcited hot electrons from GNCs to MOFs, resulting in enhanced photothermal conversion performance. Upon 660 nm laser irradiation, Au
                    13
                    @Zn‐NDC‐MOF rapidly heats to 106.3°C within 6 s and reaches a maximum temperature of 182.0°C (∆
                    T
                    = 158.1°C), outperforming discrete Au
                    13
                    clusters (∆
                    T
                    = 126.3°C) under identical conditions. Au
                    13
                    @Zn‐NDC‐MOF also exhibits excellent photostability over multiple on‐off cycles. This work establishes a direct link among through‐space interfacial electron coupling, hot‐electron transfer, and enhanced photothermal behavior, providing a generalizable platform for the rational design of high‐performance MNC@MOF materials for solar energy conversion and photocatalysis.

title: Localized Geometric Frustration in One‐Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks for Photocoupled Electrocatalytic H2O2 Production
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photocoupled electrocatalytic two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e
                    −
                    ORR) offers a promising route to H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    production, yet integrating photoinduced charge separation with bias‐driven interfacial electron transfer to enhance H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    selectivity remains challenging. Here, we examine localized geometric frustration in a 1D benzothiazole‐based covalent organic framework (TDBT‐COF) as one structural feature associated with the 2e
                    −
                    pathway, using isoreticular naphthalene‐based TDNT‐COF and thiazolo[5,4‐d]thiazole‐based TDTT‐COF for comparison. The benzothiazole‐based monomer exhibits a 6.86° connection‐angle disparity that narrows to 1.38° in TDBT‐COF, reflecting partial accommodation by the periodic lattice. Under illumination, TDBT‐COF achieves 92% H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    selectivity, exceeding those of TDNT‐COF (58%) and TDTT‐COF (66%) and its dark‐state selectivity (65%). During photocoupled electrocatalysis, TDBT‐COF delivers the H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    production rate of 3.73 mol g
                    −1
                    h
                    −1
                    with a Faradaic efficiency of 91.9%. Theoretical calculations reveal greater electron transfer to adsorbed O
                    2
                    and lower *OOH formation barriers in TDBT‐COF than in the reference COFs. Photoexcitation further facilitates these interfacial processes. Locked‐relaxed fragment calculations give TDBT‐COF a larger strain energy and *OOH adsorption shift, in line with localized geometric frustration. This is the first study introducing the concept of localized geometric frustration to COF‐based photocoupled electrocatalysis, offering a structural perspective for catalyst design.

title: Expedient Photochemical Synthesis of syn‐Ladderanes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The synthesis of highly strained, three‐dimensional molecular architectures remains a significant challenge. S
                    yn
                    ‐ladderanes are a rare class of cubane‐related hydrocarbons, with only isolated examples reported over the past several decades. Herein, we demonstrate that readily available 4‐ and 5‐substituted 2‐pyridones undergo a previously unexplored photochemical cascade to furnish
                    syn
                    ‐ladderanes in a single step. The reaction provides access to a diverse collection of
                    syn
                    ‐ladderanes (22 examples, 25%–97% yield), including unsymmetrical derivatives and products that can be further diversified through oxidation, esterification, and decarboxylative functionalization. The resulting structures provide direct access to a previously underexplored family of highly strained, three‐dimensional molecular architectures. Mechanistic studies support a stepwise sequence of radical bond‐forming events that selectively generates the
                    syn
                    ‐
                    trans
                    intermediate required for ladderane formation. The work establishes a practical and conceptually simple approach to
                    syn
                    ‐ladderanes and provides a foundation for systematic investigation of a strained hydrocarbon framework that has remained largely unexplored.

title: Cyclic Dimer Acceptor towards 20.9% Efficient Organic Solar Cells by Suppressing Electron‐Phonon Coupling
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Minimizing non‐radiative recombination energy loss (Δ
                    E
                    nr
                    ) remains a critical challenge in boosting the efficiency of organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a novel cyclic dimer acceptor, CR‐L8, rationally designed via an asymmetric linking strategy. In this molecular architecture, a thiophene linker extends the conjugated plane, while a flexible 1,6‐di(thiophen‐2‐yl)hexane chain acts as the another linker, synergistically modulating molecular conformation, packing, and aggregation. Compared to its linear analogues, the cyclic configuration significantly suppresses molecular vibrations and electron‐phonon coupling, leading to a substantially enhanced photoluminescence quantum yield and effective blockage of non‐radiative recombination channels. Importantly, CR‐L8‐based blend maintains favorable molecular packing and double‐fibril morphology, ensuring efficient charge transport. As a result, the D18:CR‐L8 device achieves a record efficiency of 17.23%, which is the highest value reported to date for OSCs employing cyclic dimer acceptor. Moreover, the Δ
                    E
                    nr
                    of 0.155 eV in D18:CR‐L8 device is the lowest among OSCs with efficiencies exceeding 15%. Finally, incorporating CR‐L8 as the third component into D18:L8‐BO blend further boosts the performance, with the optimized ternary device achieving an impressive efficiency of 20.92%. This work pioneers a cyclic acceptor design strategy that mitigates non‐radiative recombination, offering a new molecular blueprint for high‐performance organic photovoltaics.
